The request protocole: the protocol's version, Nuée's, the names of the requests, and with complet this description.

groupes.titre: Statistics and plots of the data

description: The engine is the R script moteur/serveur.R of Nuée's sources (in an installed copy, the folder moteur of its resources). It finds Nuée's root from its own path, so it can be started from any working folder; it loads the engine (moteur/charger.R, every file of moteur/R) and the R console (moteur/console.R), then listens.
Both arguments are optional: the port, 8765 by default; the folder of the interface it serves at /, app/interface of the same tree by default.

It needs R 4.6 (the checks also run on R 4.1 to 4.3) with the packages jsonlite, httpuv, openxlsx, haven, readxl, RSQLite and ranger, and R's recommended packages foreign, nlme, mgcv, MASS, rpart and cluster.
Once it listens, it writes the line PRET <port> on its standard output: a client waits for it before its first request.
It listens on 127.0.0.1 only, and answers one request at a time (R has one thread): a long computation delays the requests that follow it.

Nothing stops it but its process: a client kills it when done. On Windows, bin\Rscript.exe only starts bin\x64\Rscript.exe, which is R itself: start the latter, or stop the whole process tree (taskkill /T).

Its temporary files (pasted tables, converted .usp projects, files exported without a path, the console's plots) go in R's temporary folder, under TMPDIR, TMP or TEMP: the application gives it a folder of its own for each run and deletes it when Nuée closes.

environnement.NUEE_JETON: The session's token (see jeton). The engine removes it from its environment once read, so that neither the console nor the programs it starts inherit it.
environnement.TMPDIR, TMP, TEMP: Where R puts its temporary folder.
environnement.CONVERTISSEUR_USP: The compiled .usp converter; without it, outils/export_project.exe, else convertisseur/export_project.py run by Python.
environnement.PYTHON: The Python that runs the .usp converter when it isn't compiled (python, or python3 outside Windows).
environnement.R_LIBS: An installed copy points it at the packages it brings along (Windows, macOS); the application also starts R with --no-init-file there, so that the researcher's .Rprofile stays out.

port.description: The first argument. The desktop application asks for 47863 when it is free (the interface keeps its settings per address), else any free port; a client chooses a free port of 127.0.0.1 itself and gives it.

description: The engine answers only the requests that carry the session's token: other web pages and other users of the computer reach 127.0.0.1 too, and the R console runs what it is sent.

The token is drawn by whoever starts the engine and given to it in NUEE_JETON: the application draws 32 random bytes, written as 64 hexadecimal characters. Started without NUEE_JETON, the engine draws its own and prints the address to open in a browser, http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/connexion?jeton=<token>.

Each request carries it in the cookie nuee_<port> (cookies don't tell ports apart: one name per engine), in its Cookie header: Cookie: nuee_<port>=<token>. Without it, or with another value, the answer is 403 {"erreur": "Request refused: it doesn't come from Nuée's window."}.
The Host header must be 127.0.0.1:<port> or localhost:<port>; any other name gets 403 with the plain text interdit, even with the cookie (a site whose name points to 127.0.0.1, DNS rebinding).

langue.description: The header X-Langue: en gives the engine's messages and texts in English; without it, or with any other value, they are in French. A few requests take the language of the text they write as a parameter instead (methodes, resultats_texte, script_r, document_reproductible).

description: A request is POST /api/<name> with a JSON object of its parameters as body, in UTF-8; an empty body is a request without parameters. Neither the method nor the Content-Type is checked.

The engine reads the body with jsonlite::fromJSON(simplifyVector = TRUE): an array of numbers or strings becomes a vector, so a one-element array and its element are the same parameter; an array of objects becomes a table (a data.frame), which the requests that take a list of objects accept; an array of arrays becomes a matrix; an array mixing numbers and strings becomes strings; null is the same as leaving the parameter out.
Parameters the description doesn't list are ignored, except by moyennes and puissance_tendance, which take every parameter but modele as one of their settings.

The engine reads a parameter with R's $, which also takes a parameter whose name starts with the one read when that one is left out: without n, classes_valeurs reads nom as n. Send only the parameters a request takes.
The answer is written by jsonlite::toJSON(auto_unbox = TRUE, dataframe = "columns", na = "null", null = "null", digits = NA).

A vector of one element is written as that element: a field described as an array can arrive as a single value when it has one element, unless the engine keeps it an array (I() in its code). A table (data.frame) becomes an object of columns, each always an array; a matrix, an array of its rows; a missing value, NaN or an infinity, null; numbers keep all their digits.

Errors carry no code, only their message, said for a user in the request's language: a client tells them apart by their status (and conflit for 409), not by their words. A malformed parameter often gets R's own message, untranslated. A few requests answer 200 with an error inside: series' tendances_erreur, raster_infos' erreur for a file it can't read, test_deux_variables' erreur for a pair it can't test.

statuts.302: /api/connexion with the right token: the cookie is set and the browser sent to the interface.
statuts.400: The request failed: {"erreur": message}, the message in the request's language (an R error, often one of the engine's own, said for the user).
statuts.403: Without the session's token: {"erreur": message}. With another host name: the plain text interdit. /api/connexion with a wrong token: the plain text jeton refusé.
statuts.404: A path outside /api/ that isn't a file of the interface: the plain text introuvable.
statuts.409: enregistrer only: the file changed elsewhere since it was read or written, {"erreur": message, "conflit": true, "date": its modification time, seconds since 1970}.

chemins./api/connexion?jeton=<token>[&...]: For a browser (development): with the right token, sets the cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Path=/) and redirects (302) to /, keeping the address's other parameters (ouvrir=<path> opens a file). No cookie is needed.
chemins./api/fichier?chemin=<path>: The bytes of a file the engine wrote in its temporary folder (an export asked without chemin), as an attachment; any other path is refused (400, File not allowed). The cookie is needed.
chemins./api/televerser?nom=<file name>: The body is a file's bytes: kept in the engine's temporary folder under that name, then opened as ouvrir opens a file (its answer is ouvrir's). The cookie is needed.
chemins./api/deposer?nom=<file name>: The body is a file's bytes: kept in the engine's temporary folder under that name; answers {"chemin": its path}, for a request that takes a path (predire_fichier, the formulaire of kobo_apercu…). The cookie is needed.
chemins./: The files of the interface folder (the second argument), without the token: index.html, its scripts. Served with Cache-Control: no-cache.

client: Find R and its Rscript: on Windows, Nuée's own (resources\R\bin\x64\Rscript.exe in an installed copy) or R's (%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\R\R-4.6.2\bin\x64\Rscript.exe for a user installation), elsewhere the one on the PATH.
Choose a free port of 127.0.0.1 and draw a token (32 random bytes in hexadecimal).
Start Rscript <Nuée>/moteur/serveur.R <port> with NUEE_JETON=<token> in its environment, and preferably TMPDIR, TMP and TEMP set to a new folder of the client's.
Read its standard output until the line PRET <port>; if the process stops first, what it wrote says why (a missing package, often).

Send each request as POST http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/<name>, with the headers Cookie: nuee_<port>=<token>, Content-Type: application/json and X-Langue: en (or fr), and the parameters as a JSON object.
Read the answer: 200, the result; 400 or 409, {"erreur": …} said for a user; 403, a wrong token or host.
Ask protocole first: its version tells which requests and parameters exist (a 400 Unknown request: the engine speaks 1.0).
Projects (P1, P2…) and fitted models (M1, M2…) live in the engine's session, under the ids its answers give: they last as long as the engine, unless saved with enregistrer.
Stop the engine's process when done, and delete the temporary folder.

Colonne.description: A column of the project: a variable's number (its uid), or "id:k", the observations' k-th identifier ("id:1" their names; k as the rang of Projet's identifiants).

Groupement.description: What makes groups of observations, for a random effect, a cross-validation by groups or the time of an autocorrelation (regression.R: specs_groupement): an identifier of the observations by its name, or a variable by its number. Several arrive as an array of objects, a table for jsonlite.

by.description: "id" (an identifier) or "variable"; some requests also take "effets", the regression's random effects.

id.description: With by = "id": the identifier's name, as in Projet's identifiants (not "id:k").

pentes.description: A random effect's random slopes: the numbers of their variables.

chemin.description: The file written, or the first of them.

chemins.description: Every file written (always an array): a format without sheets writes one file per table.

Projet.description: A project's summary (serveur.R: resume_projet): what the interface shows of it, with the ids requests take.

id.description: The project's id in the session (P1, P2…): the parameter projet of other requests.

nom.description: Its name: its file's name, a sheet's name in brackets, or the name it was given.

source.description: The name of the file or table its data came from ("" when unknown).

modifie.description: Whether it has changes not saved yet.

chemin.description: The file it was opened from; null for a pasted table, the example, imported spectra or a summary by group.

table.description: The sheet or table of that file it was read from.

brut.description: A KoboToolbox or ODK export opened as it is, not imported.

annulable.description: The label of the change annuler would undo; null when there is nothing to undo.

revision.description: Counts the changes of its data and their undos: a view that keeps a computation on the data computes it again when it changes.

chemin_enregistrement.description: Where saving writes without asking: the .nuee it was saved to, or opened from.

observations.description: The observations, as columns: uid, their numbers, and nom, their names (a project of one observation gives single values).

identifiants.description: The observations' other identifiers (site, year…), each {rang, nom}: rang is the k of "id:k"; without the .usp files' internal ones ($ClassID…) and empty ones.

variables.description: The variables with data, each {uid, nom, qualitative, categories (always an array), manquantes (missing values), temps (a qualitative variable whose categories are all dates or numbers, usable as a time), unite, description}.

jeux.description: The datasets of a .usp project, each {nom, n_obs, n_var}.

modeles.description: The model definitions kept in the project.

session.description: Whether the project holds a session of the interface (its views and fitted models), saved with it.

coordonnees.description: Its coordinates (spatial.R: coordonnees_projet): {x, y, the variables' numbers; systeme, an EPSG code or "plan"; nom_x, nom_y}; null when none are set or they no longer hold.

kobo.description: The settings of the KoboToolbox or ODK import that made it, to make it again (kobo.R); null otherwise.

historique.description: The number of events in the audit trail a .usp file kept (the request historique lists them).

predictions.description: The prediction sets of a .usp project, each {nom, n_obs}.

Modele.description: A fitted model's results (serveur.R: resultat_modele for a PCA, PLS, OPLS, PLS-DA or OPLS-DA; resultat_regression for a regression; resultat_<type> of another analysis, analyses.R). The common fields first; each family adds its own, as noted.

id.description: The fitted model's id in the session (M1, M2…): the parameter modele of other requests.

nom.description: Its name (M3, or the name it was given; a refit is "M3 (1)"…).

type.description: PCA, PLS, OPLS, PLS-DA, OPLS-DA, a regression (LM, LMM, GLM, GAM) or another analysis (RDA, CA, CCA, LDA, TREE, KMEANS, INDVAL, TRIM, PCOA, NMDS, PERMANOVA, MANTEL, FOREST, BOOST, DISTANCE).

opls.description: Whether it is an OPLS or OPLS-DA.

A.description: PCA and PLS: its number of components (an OPLS: predictive and orthogonal); 0 for a regression or another analysis.

Ap.description: An OPLS's number of predictive components; 1 for a PCA or a PLS, 0 for a regression or another analysis.

K.description: Its number of X terms (a regression: the terms it kept; an analysis: its X columns).

noms_y.description: The names of its Y terms (always an array; empty for a PCA).

observations.description: A table, one row per observation of the model. PCA and PLS: t1…tA, u1…uA (PLS), T2, DModX, DModX_absolu, DModX_pondere, "<y> observé", "<y> ajusté", "<y> résidu" (PLS), classe, classe_predite, classe_predite_vc (PLS-DA), uid, nom. A regression: uid, nom, "<y> observé", "<y> ajusté", "<y> ajusté (effets fixes)" (a mixed model), "<y> prédit (VC)", residu, quantile_normal, levier and cook (LM), a column per random effect's level, groupe_vc. Another analysis: its own columns, with uid and nom.

reglages.description: Its settings in the form of the definition parameters, to modify it (nouveau.R: reglages_modele): type, x, y, classe, exclues, condition, echelles, blocs, modificateurs, transformations, A, G, vc, validation, aleatoires, correlation, famille, lisses, decalage, k_courbes, par_courbes, lisse_spatial, croises, croises_reglages, options, spectres, test, nom, titre.

numero.description: Its definition's number in the project (ajuster's numero), when the project keeps it.

app.description: Whether its definition was made by Nuée (and joins the project), not read from a .usp file.

test.description: With a test set (the definition's test): its predictions and statistics, {n, hors_domaine, observations, and for a PLS statistiques (y, n, RMSEP, biais, SEP, Q2ext) and classement (PLS-DA)} (jeu_test.R: evaluer_test; a regression's and an analysis's own). An RDA's or a CCA's test is its permutation test instead, {F, p, df, permutations}.

demande.description: The parameters it was fitted with, as the engine received them; {type, numero} for a model read from a file.

G.description: PCA, PLS, regressions and the analyses validated by groups: the number of cross-validation groups.

vc_par.description: What made the cross-validation groups (an identifier's or a variable's name); "" when the observations were dealt in turn.

composantes.description: PCA and PLS: a table, one row per component, composante, R2X, R2Xcum, R2Y and R2Ycum (PLS), Q2, Q2cum, valeur_propre; null for a regression.

variables.description: PCA and PLS: a table, one row per X term, terme, bloc, p1…pA, R2V_cum, Q2V_cum and p1_IC… (PCA), centre, poids, echelle, VIP, VIP_IC, w1, w*1… and their _IC (PLS); an RDA or a CA: its own.

variables_y.description: PLS: a table, one row per Y term, terme, bloc, c1…cA and their _IC, R2V_cum, Q2V_cum, centre, poids, RMSEE, RMSEcv.

coefficients.description: PLS: a table, one row per X term then Constante: terme, and for each Y "CoeffCS <y>" (centred and scaled), "Coeff <y>" (in the data's units) and each one's "… IC" (jack-knife half-width).

limites.description: PCA and PLS: the limits T2Crit(95%), T2Crit(99%) and, with more terms than components, DCrit(5%).

RMSEE.description: PLS, regressions and some analyses: by Y name, the root mean square error of estimation.

RMSEcv.description: By Y name, the root mean square error of cross-validation.

seuil_vip.description: PLS: the VIP threshold found, {seuil, chute, marche, retenues}: the threshold, the drop at it, whether that drop is a clear step, the terms above it (statistiques.R: seuil_vip).

variance_t.description: PCA and PLS: each component's score variance.

ellipse.description: PCA and PLS: the squared radii of Hotelling's T² ellipse of a score plot, {95, 99}.

validation.description: PCA and PLS: how it was cross-validated, centres, sans_fuite or complet.

gardes_vc.description: PCA and PLS validated sans_fuite: the terms that kept the full model's weight in a cross-validation sub-model, with the group and the share of their standard deviation they kept (validation_croisee.R: gardes_vc); null when none did.

q2_vide.description: PLS and OPLS validated with recomputed centres: the Q2 of the empty model (each group predicted by the mean of the others).

gain.description: The model's gain over the empty model, (Q2cum − q2_vide) / (1 − q2_vide).

hierarchique.description: A PLS whose X are scores of other models: its honest Q2, each base model refitted without the hidden group (hierarchique.R: q2_hierarchique); null otherwise.

stocke.description: The components a .usp file stored with the model, as arrays R2X, R2Xcum, R2Y, R2Ycum, Q2, Q2cum.

version_origine.description: The version of the program that made a model read from a file.

groupe.description: A class model (modeles_classe): its group's name.

classe_modele.description: A class model: its class (the category it was fitted on).

cv_anova.description: PLS: by Y name, its CV-ANOVA table {source, SS, DF, MS, F, p, SD}.

classification.description: PLS-DA: its classification, fitted and cross-validated, {ajuste, vc}.

regression.description: true for a regression, false for another analysis; absent for a PCA or a PLS.

transformation_y.description: Regressions (and trees): the response's transformation, "" for none.

coefficients_regression.description: Regressions: a table, one row per coefficient, terme, estimation, erreur_type, ddl, t, p, bas, haut (the 95 % interval).

termes_retires.description: Regressions: the terms left out as redundant (a qualitative variable's reference category…).

termes_absents.description: Regressions: the combinations of categories never observed.

qualite.description: Regressions: the fit's quality, r2 and r2_ajuste (LM), marginal and conditionnel (mixed), or deviance_expliquee (GLM, GAM), then AIC, AICc, BIC, logLik, parametres, Q2, RMSEcv, echecs_vc, sans_categorie_vc, facteurs_vc; trees and some analyses: their own.

parametre_loi.description: Regressions with a distribution that has one: its estimated parameter (the negative binomial's θ, Tweedie's p, the zero-inflated Poisson's θ1 and θ2, the beta's φ).

courbes.description: A GAM: a table of its curves (edf, test).

decalage.description: GLM and GAM: the effort variable's name, with an offset.

dispersion.description: A Poisson model: its Pearson dispersion (χ² over the residual degrees of freedom).

gamm.description: Regressions: fitted by mgcv::gamm (a normal GLM or GAM with random effects and CAR1).

dans.description: With CAR1 in a finer level than the random effects: that level's name.

variances.description: Mixed models: a table of the random effects' variances, composante, terme, variance, correlation.

phi.description: With CAR1: its estimated correlation φ.

niveaux.description: Regressions: the random effects' levels, the widest first.

exclues_manquantes.description: Regressions and analyses: the observations left out for a missing value.

pentes.description: Regressions: the terms with a random slope, an array per random effect's level.

parts_variance.description: Mixed models: each level's share of the variance.

singularites.description: Mixed models with random slopes: the signs of a singular fit.

qualitatives.description: Regressions: the qualitative variables, those with adjusted means (moyennes).

signature.description: Regressions: what the AIC can compare (the response, its transformation, the observations, the kind of distribution and likelihood): two models of the same signature have comparable AICs.

prediction.description: Another analysis: whether it predicts new observations (predire).

chiffres.description: Another analysis: its line of figures for the explorer ("R2 0.70 · Q2 0.52 · 3 leaves").

vues_defaut.description: Another analysis: the views the interface opens first.

ResumeModele.description: A model definition kept in a project (serveur.R: resume_modele).

numero.description: Its number in the project (3 for M3): the parameter numero of ajuster.

nom.description: Its name (M3, or the name it was given).

type.description: PCA, PLS, OPLS, PLS-DA, OPLS-DA, a regression (LM, LMM, GLM, GAM) or another analysis (RDA, CA, CCA, LDA, TREE, KMEANS, INDVAL, TRIM, PCOA, NMDS, PERMANOVA, MANTEL, FOREST, BOOST, DISTANCE).

A.description: Its number of components (0: chosen when fitted, or none).

ajuste.description: Whether it was fitted (in the file it came from, or by Nuée).

erreur.description: Why it couldn't be fitted, when it couldn't.

x.description: The names of its X terms (without a regression's factors that have no main effect).

y.description: The names of its Y terms.

stocke.description: The components a .usp file stored with it, as arrays: R2X, R2Xcum, R2Y, R2Ycum, Q2, Q2cum; null without them.

version_origine.description: The version of the program that made it, for a model from a file.

EtatFichier.description: What the engine knows of a project's file when it read or wrote it, to see before writing over it whether it changed since (serveur.R: etat_fichier).

chemin.description: The file's path, made absolute, with / as separator.

date.description: Its modification time, in seconds since 1970.

EntreeJournal.description: An entry of the R console's log (console.R: noter); the engine keeps the last 1,500 to 2,000.

n.description: Its number: entries are numbered from 1 in the order they are written.

type.description: appel (an engine call the interface made, written in R), resultat (what R prints of a model just fitted), commande (a console command), sortie (its output), avertissement (a warning), erreur (an error, a console command's or a request's), image (a plot).

heure.description: The time it was written, hh:mm:ss.

texte.description: Its text, lines joined by \n; for an image, a data:image/png;base64 address.

ApercuKobo.description: The preview of the import of a KoboToolbox or ODK Central export with given settings (kobo.R: apercu_collecte), what the import dialog shows.

tables.description: The export's tables, the submissions table first, each {nom, lignes (its rows), parent (its parent table's name, null for the submissions table), principale (whether it is the submissions table), niveau (how many parent tables it has above it)}.

colonnes.description: The number of columns the import gives.

principale.description: Whether that table is the submissions table.

metadonnees.description: The metadata that can be kept, one per role present in the table or its parent tables, each {role, colonnes (always an array), garde (whether it is kept), nom (the role in words, in the request's language)}.

retirees.description: The metadata columns dropped (always an array).

parents.description: One per parent table of the imported table, nearest first, each {table, colonnes (the columns its import gives, which can be joined; always an array), choisies (those joined; always an array)}.

formulaire.description: The XLSForm form given: {fichier, titre, langues (its label languages, "" for the label column; always an array), langue (the one used)}; null without a form.

coordonnees.description: Whether the import gives the project coordinates (a GPS point, in WGS 84).

phrases.description: What the import does, one sentence per change, in the request's language (always an array).

Coordonnees.description: A project's coordinates as they are set and still hold (spatial.R: coordonnees_projet): two different quantitative variables and their system.

x.description: The number of the variable that holds x (the east, or the longitude).

y.description: The number of the variable that holds y (the north, or the latitude).

systeme.description: Their system: an EPSG code Nuée knows (4326, 2154…), or "plan" for plane coordinates in metres of an unstated system.

nom_x.description: The name of the x variable.

nom_y.description: The name of the y variable.

type.description: The model's type. Any other value is fitted as a PLS, without an error; verifier also takes CLASSES (the class models' PCA, without the class).

valeurs.PLS-DA: PLS discriminant analysis, its Y the categories of classe
valeurs.OPLS: orthogonal PLS, as many predictive components as Y
valeurs.OPLS-DA: orthogonal PLS-DA, as many predictive components as classes less one

x.description: The X variables' numbers (a qualitative variable enters by its categories). A PCA, PLS or OPLS needs at least one; a regression without X is the intercept-only model; another analysis reads the roles it needs. With spectres, they are taken in the table's order.

y.description: The Y variables' numbers: PLS and OPLS (one or more), a regression (exactly one, quantitative), an analysis with responses (RDA, CCA…). A PLS-DA takes classe instead.

classe.description: PLS-DA and OPLS-DA: the qualitative variable whose categories are the classes (only the observations of a known class enter); LDA and a classification tree: their class variable.

exclues.description: The observations left out of the model (unticked), by their numbers (Projet's observations.uid).

echelle.description: The scaling of the terms that have none in echelles.

valeurs.UV: centred and divided by the standard deviation
valeurs.Par: Pareto: centred and divided by the square root of the standard deviation

A.description: PCA, PLS and OPLS: the number of components; 0 chooses it by the automatic fit (nouveau.R: autoajuster, cross-validation and the published rules). An OPLS has at least its predictive ones. Ignored by regressions and the other analyses.

nom.description: The model's name; by default M<n + 1>, n the number of definitions in the project. A definition of the project with that name is replaced by this one (Model › Modify model).

G.description: Without vc: the number of cross-validation groups, the observations dealt to them in turn.

transformations.description: By variable, its transformation: {"<variable number>": "racine2" | "racine4" | "log10" | "log10:C2" for log10(x + C2) | "ln:C1:C2", "neglog:C1:C2" (−log10), "exp:C1:C2", "lineaire:C1:C2" or "log10:C1:C2" of C1·x + C2 | "logit:C1:C2" between the bounds C1 < C2 | "puissance:C1:C2:C3" for (C1·x + C2)^C3, "puissance:C3"}. A qualitative variable isn't transformed.

croises.description: Cross terms and powers, each the numbers of two or more X variables: [[3, 5], [4, 4]] for v3·v5 and v4². A qualitative variable enters once at most, by each of its categories. In a regression, a factor that isn't in x enters without a main effect (y ~ a + a:b).

croises_reglages.description: By cross term, named by its variables' numbers in order ("3*5"): {echelle, bloc, modificateur}; without it, the default scaling, neither block nor modifier.

spectres.description: Spectral preprocessing, applied in order to each observation's quantitative X: {type: "snv"}, {type: "msc"}, {type: "sg", derivee (0), fenetre (11: odd, 3 or more), degre (2)}, {type: "detrend", degre (2)}, {type: "ligne_base"} (spectres.R). Not for a regression.

test.description: The observations of a test set: left out of the model, then predicted by it (Modele's test). The analyses that don't predict refuse one.

vc.description: What makes the cross-validation groups: an identifier ({by: "id", id: its name}) or a variable ({by: "variable", variable: its number}), one group per value; absent, or {by: "order"}: G groups in turn. A mixed model without it is validated by its first random effect.

blocs.description: By variable, the name of its block: block weighting, each term's weight divided by the square root of its block's number of terms; in a regression, only the groups of the contributions table (apports).

modificateurs.description: By variable, a factor multiplying its weight (1: none).

aleatoires.description: Regressions: the random effects, nested from the widest to the finest, three at most, each an identifier or a qualitative variable; its pentes: the quantitative X variables (terms on their own) with a random slope at that level. An LMM needs one, an LM takes none.

correlation.description: Regressions with random effects: {type: "CAR1", temps: a Groupement, the time (an identifier or a quantitative variable), dans: a Groupement, a finer level than the last random effect (optional)}: a CAR1 autocorrelation within those groups, a single time per group. A GLM or GAM takes it only with the normal distribution (mgcv::gamm).

famille.description: GLM and GAM: the response's distribution.

lisses.description: GAM: the quantitative X variables fitted as smooth curves, s(x).

decalage.description: GLM and GAM with a log link (poisson, binomiale_negative, gamma, tweedie, poisson_zi): the effort variable, offset(log(effort)).

k_courbes.description: GAM: by curve's variable, its basis dimension k, a whole number from 3 to 100 (10 at most without it).

par_courbes.description: GAM: by curve's variable, the number of a qualitative X variable that is also a term of the model: a curve per category, s(x, by = f).

lisse_spatial.description: GAM: a spatial smooth of two quantitative coordinates, {variables: [x, y], base: "tp" (thin plate, the default) or "sos" (on the sphere, longitudes and latitudes in degrees), k: a whole number from 5 to 300}.

options.description: Another analysis's own settings, which its ajuster_<type> reads (analyses.R).

condition.description: Keep only the observations where this R expression is true (condition.R: the project's variables and identifiers, numbers, text and a fixed list of functions), evaluated again at each fit; a missing value counts as false.

validation.description: PCA, PLS and OPLS: how cross-validation is done; any other value is centres.

valeurs.centres: only the centres recomputed without the hidden group
valeurs.sans_fuite: centres and weights recomputed; a term nearly constant without the group keeps the full model's weight
valeurs.complet: the full model's centres and weights, as the .usp files validate

table.description: The export's table to import, as ApercuKobo's tables name it; the submissions table by default.

garder.description: The roles of the metadata to keep; the other metadata columns are dropped.

valeurs.releve: the start, end and day of the survey

parents.description: For each parent table of the imported table, by its name, the columns of its import to join to each row (as ApercuKobo's parents list them); a parent table left out joins all its columns, and without parents every one does.

formulaire.description: The path of the XLSForm form (.xlsx, .xlsm, .xls) the export was made with, which gives the labels, the categories' order and the multiple choices' 0/1 columns; none when absent or "".

langue.description: With formulaire, the language of its labels, one of the form's ("" for its label column); by default the request's language if the form has it, else its default_language, else its label column, else its first language.

projet_inconnu.quand: projet isn't the id of a project open in the session.

modele_inconnu.quand: modele isn't the id of a model fitted in the session.

modele_perime.message: The categories of <variable> changed since <model> was fitted: fit it again (Model › Modify model, or a double-click on its definition in the explorer).
modele_perime.quand: The request uses the model's data (to refit, predict or compute again) and a category the model saw was renamed, merged or emptied since, or a variable it used is no longer qualitative (serveur.R: modele with a_jour, atelier.R: aligner_categories).

regression_seulement.quand: The model isn't a regression (LM, LMM, GLM, GAM).

composantes_seulement.message: This isn't for this model: a regression or another analysis doesn't have the components and scores of a PCA or a PLS.
composantes_seulement.quand: A request that needs components and scores (serveur.R: SANS_REGRESSION: hca, permutations, scores_en_variables, appartenance, contributions, spectres, biplot, ipls) names a regression or another analysis in modele or modeles; checked before the request runs.

variable_introuvable.quand: A variable's number isn't one of the project's (nouveau.R: variable_du_projet).

identifiant_inconnu.quand: "id:k" names no identifier of the observations (variables.R: colonne_ou_identifiant).

format_inconnu.quand: The file's extension isn't one Nuée reads.

pas_de_tableau.message: The clipboard holds no table (at least two rows and two columns)
pas_de_tableau.quand: The pasted text has no tab, semicolon or comma, or a single line.

demande_inconnue.quand: /api/<name> names no request of the engine (an engine older than the request: see depuis).

jeton_refuse.message: Request refused: it doesn't come from Nuée's window.
jeton_refuse.quand: The request doesn't carry the session's token in the cookie nuee_<port>.

fichier_occupe.message: Couldn't replace <path>: another program is using it (sync, antivirus, the file open elsewhere), or it is read-only. The file was left as it was; try again, or save under another name.
fichier_occupe.quand: The file just written couldn't take the place of the old one within five seconds (nouveau.R: ecrire_sans_risque).

tableau_vide.quand: The table read has no row or no column (nouveau.R: projet_depuis_tableau).

valeurs_decalees.message: <lines>: more values than the first line has columns (<number>). The values would be shifted: a value may contain the separator (<separator>) or a quote, or a column name is missing from the first line.
valeurs_decalees.quand: Lines of a delimited text have more values than its first line has names (formats.R).

pas_un_export.message: <file> isn't a KoboToolbox or ODK Central export: it doesn't have their columns (_id, _uuid, _submission_time, _index…; SubmissionDate, KEY, meta-instanceID…). Open it with File › Open.
pas_un_export.quand: The file was given as an export but doesn't have two of their metadata columns (kobo.R: kobo_refus_export).

formulaire_pas_export.message: <file> is an XLSForm form (survey and choices sheets), not the data: give it as the form, beside the export of the data.
formulaire_pas_export.quand: A workbook with survey and choices sheets was given as the export.

zip_sans_csv.message: <file> holds no CSV file: it isn't an ODK Central export.
zip_sans_csv.quand: A .zip without a CSV file (outside media/) was given as an ODK Central export.

table_export_inconnue.message: Unknown table in the export: “<table>” (it has: “<table>”, …).
table_export_inconnue.quand: table isn't one of the export's tables.

metadonnee_inconnue.message: Unknown metadata: <role> (one can keep: envoi, auteur, identifiant, releve, validation).
metadonnee_inconnue.quand: garder names a role that isn't one of these.

pas_un_formulaire.message: <file> isn't an XLSForm form: an Excel workbook with a “survey” sheet (and “choices”) is needed.
pas_un_formulaire.quand: formulaire isn't an Excel workbook with a survey sheet.

langue_formulaire_inconnue.message: The form doesn't have the language “<language>”; it has: “<language>”, ….
langue_formulaire_inconnue.quand: langue isn't one of the form's label languages.

formulaire_sans_rapport.message: The form <file> doesn't match this export: none of its questions is a column of the table “<table>”.
formulaire_sans_rapport.quand: The form given isn't the one the export was made with.

table_parente_inconnue.message: “<table>” isn't a parent table of “<table>” (its parent tables: “<table>”, …).
table_parente_inconnue.quand: parents names a table that isn't a parent of the imported table.

colonne_parente_inconnue.quand: parents names a column that the parent table's import doesn't give.

sans_coordonnees.message: This project has no coordinates: choose them in Plots › Map (two variables and their system).
sans_coordonnees.quand: The request needs the observations' coordinates and the project has none set, or they no longer hold: a variable gone or made qualitative (spatial.R: coordonnees_projet with exiger).

variable_sans_donnees.quand: A variable's number isn't a column of the project's data (variables.R: modifier_valeur, atelier.R: coller_cellules).

nom_variable_manquant.message: Give the new variable a name
nom_variable_manquant.quand: nom is empty, or only spaces.

nom_variable_pris.quand: nom, without the spaces around it, is the name of one of the project's variables.

format_export_inconnu.quand: The extension of chemin (or format) isn't one the engine writes: xlsx, csv, tsv, txt, rds, rdata, rda, sav, dta, xpt, omv, dbf, arff (formats.R: ecrire_tableau).

classe_requise.message: A PLS-DA needs a class variable
classe_requise.quand: A PLS-DA or OPLS-DA definition without classe.

echelle_inconnue.quand: echelle or a value of echelles isn't UV, Par, Ctr or none.

transformation_inconnue.quand: A value of transformations isn't one of the forms Nuée reads (nouveau.R: lire_transformation).

croise_hors_x.message: A cross term can only use X variables
croise_hors_x.quand: A cross term of a PCA, PLS or OPLS uses a variable that isn't in x.

condition_refusee.message: "<function>" isn't allowed in a condition: comparisons (==, !=, <, >=…), &, |, !, %in%, is.na(), ifelse(), arithmetic (+, log10()…) and the group and lag functions of New variable formulas (group_mean(), previous()…).
condition_refusee.quand: The condition calls another function; it may also be unreadable, name an unknown variable or not give one logical value per observation (condition_observations lists those messages).

condition_aucune.message: None of the <n> ticked observations meets the condition <condition>.
condition_aucune.quand: The condition keeps none of the model's ticked observations.

sans_test.message: This analysis doesn't predict left-out observations: it takes no test set.
sans_test.quand: A test set for an analysis that doesn't predict (RDA, CA…).

regression_une_reponse.message: A regression needs a single Y variable, a quantitative one.
regression_une_reponse.quand: A regression's y is empty, has several variables or a qualitative one.

mixte_sans_aleatoire.message: A mixed model needs at least one random effect.

loi_inconnue.quand: famille isn't one of the distributions Nuée fits.

vc_un_groupe.message: Cross-validation by "<groups>": the model's observations have a single value, so a single group. At least two are needed.
vc_un_groupe.quand: vc's identifier or variable has one value on the model's observations.

aucune_variation.message: No component is possible: the data have no variation (constant variables, or all zero after the spectral preprocessing).
aucune_variation.quand: A PCA, PLS or OPLS whose data leave nothing to describe.

trop_de_composantes.message: Component <a> is not possible: no variation is left to describe after <n> component(s). This model can have at most <n>.
trop_de_composantes.quand: A was set above what the data allow.

ne_predit_pas.message: This analysis doesn't predict new observations.
ne_predit_pas.quand: The model is an analysis that doesn't predict (Modele's prediction false: RDA, CA, PCoA…).

temps_refuse.message: The time (<time>) must be numbers (the year) or dates (2019-05-14, 14/05/2019)<, not both>: <why>
temps_refuse.quand: A value of the time is neither a number nor a date, or numbers and dates are mixed (variables.R: temps_en_nombres, refus_temps); <why> names the first value refused: “<value>” is a number among dates, a date among numbers, isn't a date that exists, or is neither a number nor a date.

test_inconnu.quand: test isn't one of the request's tests.

cle_en_double.message: <level> has several rows for the same value of <key> (<values>): the pairing key must identify one row per level
cle_en_double.quand: In a paired test, one of the two levels compared has two rows with the same key (comparaisons.R: paires_cle).

permutations_requises.message: These tests need permutations: choose a number of them (Edit model).
permutations_requises.quand: The RDA or CCA was fitted without permutations (its options' permutations is 0).

rda_seulement.message: Only for an RDA or a CCA.
rda_seulement.quand: modele isn't a redundancy analysis (RDA) or a canonical correspondence analysis (CCA).

protocole.but: Gives the protocol's version, Nuée's version and the names of the requests the engine answers, and with complet this whole description.

complet.description: true to also get the full description (moteur/protocole.json) in description.

nuee.description: Nuée's version (app/package.json); null when the engine runs without the application's files.

demandes.description: The names of the requests this engine answers, sorted (always an array).

description.description: With complet: this description, as moteur/protocole.json holds it.

version.but: Gives the versions of R and of the R packages the engine runs on, and the system it runs on.

systeme.description: The operating system's version, as R gives it ("" when unknown).

paquets.description: The version of each of jsonlite, httpuv, openxlsx, haven, readxl, foreign, RSQLite, rmarkdown and knitr, "-" for one that isn't installed.

etat.but: Gives everything the session has open, each project's summary and each fitted model's results, as a new window of the application needs them.

projets.description: The open projects, in the order they were opened (always an array).

modeles.description: The models fitted in the session, in the order they were fitted (always an array).

projets_modifies.but: Gives the names of the open projects that have changes not saved yet, which the application asks before closing.

noms.description: Their names (always an array, empty when every project is saved).

donnees.but: Gives a project's data table for the Data view: its observations, its variables and the values of those asked.

colonnes.description: The numbers of the variables whose values to send (a view of spectra sends only the first ones, or those its filter keeps); the others come as null. Without it, all of them.

observations.description: The observations' names, in the data table's order.

uid_observations.description: Their numbers, in the same order.

variables.description: The names of the variables that have data.

uid_variables.description: Their numbers, in the same order.

valeurs.description: One element per variable, in the same order: its values for each observation (numbers; a qualitative variable's category names; null for a missing value), or null for a variable colonnes leaves out.

valeurs.but: Gives the values of one variable, or of one identifier of the observations, for the observations asked.

variable.description: The variable's number; required unless identifiant is given.

identifiant.description: Instead of a variable, the rank k of an identifier of the observations (Projet's identifiants' rang; 1 for their names): a number, not "id:k".

observations.description: The numbers of the observations whose values to give, in the order wanted; without it, no value.

variable.description: The variable's number (absent for an identifier).

nom.description: The variable's name (absent for an identifier).

valeurs.description: The value of each observation asked, in their order: a number, a category's name or an identifier's text; null for a missing value or an observation the project doesn't have.

qualitative.description: Whether the values are text: a qualitative variable, or an identifier (always true).

historique.but: Gives the audit trail a .usp project's file kept, one row per event.

resultat.description: A table as columns, each always an array, one row per event of the file's work sessions; {} when the file kept no audit trail (projet.R: historique_projet).

date.description: When it happened, YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm when the file's day/month/year or month/day/year date could be read, else as the file writes it.

logiciel.description: The program of the work session.

modele.description: The number of the model the event names ("model no. 4"), null when it names none.

session.but: Gives the interface's session kept with a project (its views and fitted models), as the JSON text the interface wrote.

session.description: The session, JSON text only the interface reads; null when the project holds none.

modeles.but: Lists the models fitted in the session, with their project and name.

resultat.description: One object per fitted model, in the order they were fitted (always an array, empty when none is fitted).

nom.description: Its definition's name, or its id when it has none.

annuler.but: Undoes the last change of a project that has an undo step, as Edit › Undo (Ctrl+Z) does.

projet.description: The project as it was before that change.

etiquette.description: The label of the change undone ("variable ratio"…), as Projet's annulable gave it.

erreurs.message: Nothing to undo
erreurs.quand: The project has no undo step left (also for an id that is no project's).

annuler.effet_detail: The project goes back to its state before its last change that has an undo step (20 are kept per project), and that step leaves the stack: there is no redo. Its documents, figures and the state of its file stay as they are now, and it counts as modified; the session's models whose observations came from a condition of the project follow its condition back.

enregistrer.but: Saves a project as a .nuee file, with the interface's session.

chemin.description: The file to write (a .nuee). Without it, <project's name>.nuee in the engine's temporary folder, for a browser to fetch with /api/fichier; the project counts as saved all the same.

session.description: The interface's session (its views and fitted models), JSON text only it reads: kept with the project and saved with it.

ecraser.description: true to write even when chemin is the project's file and that file changed elsewhere since the project read or wrote it.

version.description: Nuée's version, written in the file (its nuee field) with R's and the packages'.

chemin.description: The file written.

erreurs.message: <file> was changed elsewhere since you opened or saved it.
erreurs.quand: chemin is the file the project was read from or last saved to, it changed since (its size or modification time), and ecraser isn't true. The answer is HTTP 409: {"erreur", "conflit": true, "date": the file's modification time in seconds since 1970}.

erreurs.message: <R's own message>
erreurs.quand: The file can't be written, its folder missing for instance ("cannot open the connection", untranslated).

enregistrer.effet_detail: Writes the file, replacing an old one only once the new one is whole, and marks the project saved; with chemin, later saves go there and the file's state is kept to see a change made elsewhere. The session given is kept with the project.

sauvegarde_secours.but: Writes a recovery copy of a project without changing its state.

chemin.description: The copy to write (a .nuee), in the interface's recovery folder.

session.description: The interface's session, JSON text, written in the copy only.

version.description: Nuée's version, written in the copy.

chemin.description: The copy written, as given.

lu.description: The state of the project's file when the project read or last saved it, which the interface keeps with the copy and gives back to ouvrir (lu); null when it never read or saved a .nuee or .json.

erreurs.message: <R's own message>
erreurs.quand: chemin is missing ("a character vector argument expected") or can't be written ("cannot open the connection"), untranslated.

sauvegarde_secours.effet_detail: Writes the copy at chemin; the project, its session and its unsaved state stay as they are.

projet_texte.but: Gives a project as saving would write it, as text, for a problem report.

version.description: Nuée's version, written in the text as in a saved file.

nom.description: A file name made from the project's name, without extension (characters other than letters, digits, _, space, brackets and - become _).

texte.description: The .nuee file's JSON text, the project's session included.

projet_texte.effet_detail: Writes the project in a temporary file, reads it and deletes it.

fermer_projet.but: Closes a project: it leaves the session with the models fitted on it.

projet.description: The project's id. An id that is no project's closes nothing, without an error.

fermer_projet.effet_detail: The project and its fitted models leave the session, saved or not; its undo steps stay in the engine, unused.

ouvrir.but: Opens a file as a new project: a Nuée project, a .usp project, a table, spectra, or a KoboToolbox or ODK export.

chemin.description: The file to open, a path the engine can read: a project (.nuee, .json), a .usp project (converted first by convertisseur/export_project), a table (.csv, .txt, .tsv, .tab, .dat, .xlsx, .xlsm, .xls, .rds, .rdata, .rda, .sav, .zsav, .por, .dta, .sas7bdat, .xpt, .omv, .dbf, .arff, .gpkg), spectra (.jdx, .dx, .jcm, .spc) or an ODK Central .zip.

table.description: The sheet (Excel), object (.rds, .RData), layer (GeoPackage) or table of an ODK .zip to open, as it is written (a KoboToolbox or ODK export given a table isn't previewed); without it, a file holding several answers choisir.

brut.description: true to open a KoboToolbox or ODK export as it is written, as any table, instead of answering its import's preview.

collecte.description: true when the file must be a KoboToolbox or ODK Central export (File › Import from KoboToolbox or ODK): its import's preview is answered, and any other file refused.

kobo.description: An import's settings, the parameters of the set import_kobo as Projet's kobo gives them ({table, garder, parents, formulaire, langue}): the export is imported with them at once, without its preview (to make an import again after the engine restarted).

secours.description: true when chemin is a recovery copy (sauvegarde_secours), reopened as the project it keeps: marked modified, and the copy itself never its file.

origine.description: With secours, the project's own file, where it saves or where it came from, which becomes its chemin (a .nuee or .json also its chemin_enregistrement); given without secours, it does the same.

nom.description: With secours or origine, the project's name; by default the name of origine's file, else of the copy.

lu.description: With secours, the state of origine's file when the project read or last saved it (sauvegarde_secours's lu), so that saving over a file changed elsewhere since still asks first; ignored when its chemin isn't origine's.

resultat.description: The new project's summary; or, when chemin holds several tables and table isn't given, {choisir, chemin, nom (the file's name)}; or, for a KoboToolbox or ODK export (or with collecte), {kobo, chemin, nom}, its import's preview with the default settings, and nothing opened. With kobo, the imported project's summary with collecte.

note.description: What to know about the reading (values read as missing, short lines…) and a project saved by a newer Nuée; always an array, present only when there is something to say, and never with secours or origine.

collecte.description: With kobo, what the import did: {coordonnees (whether it set the project's coordinates), lignes, colonnes, phrases (one sentence per change, in the request's language; always an array)}.

choisir.description: Instead of a project, the file's tables to choose from (always an array), to ask again with table.

kobo.description: Instead of a project, the import's preview, to ask kobo_importer or kobo_apercu with the settings chosen, or ouvrir with brut.

erreurs.message: The .usp file couldn't be converted: <the converter's output>
erreurs.quand: The .usp converter (outils/export_project.exe, or Python with convertisseur/export_project.py) wrote no JSON.

erreurs.message: This file holds no table (data frame or matrix)
erreurs.quand: An R file (.rds, .RData) holds no table.

erreurs.message: Table not found in the file: <table>
erreurs.quand: table isn't an object of the R file (an unknown sheet of a workbook gets readxl's own Sheet '<table>' not found).

erreurs.message: Nuée opens .rds and .RData files only with R 4.4 or newer (before, such a file can run code as soon as it is read). This R is version <version>: save the table in another format (CSV, Excel...), or install a newer R.
erreurs.quand: An R file, with an R older than 4.4.

erreurs.message: This R file holds an object Nuée doesn't open (environment, function, S4, R5 or R6 object...): reading it could run code. Save a data frame, a matrix or a list of data frames in it.
erreurs.quand: An R file whose object isn't made only of vectors and lists.

erreurs.message: <the reader's own message>
erreurs.quand: The file doesn't exist or can't be read: R's or its package's message (readxl, haven, jsonlite…), untranslated.

ouvrir.effet_detail: Opens a new project (with secours or origine, marked modified). A file with several tables, or a KoboToolbox or ODK export to preview, opens nothing; the export's reading is kept in a cache.

exemple.but: Opens the example project (made-up data) in the request's language, as a new project without a file.

resultat.description: exemple/orchards.json with X-Langue: en, else exemple/vergers.json (the same apples, exemple/creer_exemple.js); its chemin is null, so that saving asks where.

exemple.effet_detail: Opens a new project, not modified.

coller.but: Opens a table pasted from a spreadsheet as a new project.

texte.description: The pasted cells: one line per observation, the first with the columns' names, separated by tabs (or semicolons or commas).

nom.description: The new project's name.

fichier_colle.description: The file of the engine's temporary folder that keeps the pasted text (tableau colle.tsv), which the console's log reads.

note.description: What to know about the reading (values read as missing…), always an array.

coller.effet_detail: Opens a new project, marked modified (it has no file); the pasted text is kept in a file of the engine's temporary folder.

importer_spectres.but: Opens spectra from one or more files (JCAMP-DX, SPC, text) as one new project, with a table of information on the samples if given.

chemins.description: The spectra files (.jdx, .dx, .jcm, .spc, or text: a column of x values, then one column per spectrum), each giving one spectrum or several.

infos.description: A table of information on the samples (concentrations, classes…), any format File › Open reads, its first column the spectra's file names, joined to them.

nom.description: The new project's name; by default the file's name for one file, "Spectres (<n> fichiers)" for several.

note.description: What to know (spectra interpolated on the first one's x values, spectra without information, information without a spectrum), always an array.

erreurs.message: <file>: <the reader's message>
erreurs.quand: A file can't be read as spectra.

erreurs.message: No readable spectrum in <file>
erreurs.quand: A file holds no spectrum.

erreurs.message: A spectrum of fewer than two values in <file>
erreurs.quand: A spectrum has fewer than two x values.

erreurs.message: Missing or unreadable x values in <file>
erreurs.quand: A spectrum has x values that aren't finite numbers.

erreurs.message: The spectra don't have the same units (<x values|y values>): <units>
erreurs.quand: The files give different units for the x or y values.

erreurs.message: The spectra have no x values in common
erreurs.quand: Spectra on different x values don't overlap over two values.

erreurs.message: No spectrum
erreurs.quand: chemins is empty.

erreurs.message: No name in the first column of the information table matches a spectrum (its file name)
erreurs.quand: With infos, none of its first column's names is a spectrum's.

importer_spectres.effet_detail: Opens a new project, marked modified (it has no file).

kobo_apercu.but: Previews the import of a KoboToolbox or ODK Central export with the given settings, without opening anything.

chemin.description: The export: a KoboToolbox workbook (.xlsx, a sheet per repeat group) or CSV, or an ODK Central .zip (one CSV per table) or submissions CSV.

kobo_apercu.effet_detail: Opens nothing: only the readings of the export and of the form are kept in a cache (the last four, by file path, size and date).

kobo_importer.but: Imports a table of a KoboToolbox or ODK Central export as a new project, with the given settings.

chemin.description: The export, as for kobo_apercu.

nom.description: The file name the project's name is made from (with a repeat group's name in brackets, "export (observation).xlsx"); chemin's file name by default.

resultat.description: The new project; its kobo gives the settings to make the import again, its collecte (saved with it) where the data came from, for the Methods text.

note.description: What to know about the reading, always an array, present only when there is something to say.

collecte.description: What the import did: {coordonnees (whether it set the project's coordinates), lignes, colonnes, phrases (one sentence per change, in the request's language; always an array)}.

kobo_importer.effet_detail: Opens a new project, not modified; its import's settings are kept with it for the session only (Projet's kobo), not in its file.

modifier_valeur.but: Changes one value of the data, as typing in a cell of the Data view does.

observation.description: The observation's number (the uid of Projet's observations).

valeur.description: The new value, as text, without the spaces around it: empty (or absent), the value becomes missing; for a qualitative variable, a category's name (one it doesn't have yet is added after the others); for a quantitative one, a number, with a decimal point or comma (3.5 or 3,5).

resultat.description: The project after the change.

erreurs.message: Non-numeric value for <variable>: <value>
erreurs.quand: The variable is quantitative and the value isn't a number.

erreurs.message: subscript out of bounds
erreurs.quand: observation isn't one of the project's observations (R's own message).

modifier_valeur.effet_detail: One undo step, labelled in French whatever the language (modification de <variable>); the models already fitted keep their results until they are fitted again.

coller_cellules.but: Pastes a block of cells into the data from a chosen cell, as Ctrl+V in the Data view does.

observations.description: The block's rows: the observations' numbers, in the view's order.

variables.description: Its columns: the variables' numbers, in the view's order.

valeurs.description: Its cells as text, one array per row, one element per column; null leaves a cell as it is, "" makes it missing. Each cell as modifier_valeur reads it: a qualitative variable takes a category's name (new ones added in the order they come), a quantitative one a number (3,5 or 3.5).

resultat.description: The project after the paste.

collage.description: {cellules: the number of cells that changed}.

erreurs.message: The pasted block must have one row per observation and one column per variable.
erreurs.quand: valeurs doesn't have the shape of observations × variables.

erreurs.message: Non-numeric value for <variable>: <value> (observation <name>)
erreurs.quand: A cell of a quantitative variable isn't a number: nothing changes.

erreurs.message: subscript out of bounds
erreurs.quand: One of the observations isn't the project's (R's own message).

coller_cellules.effet_detail: One undo step (pasted cells), even when no cell changes.

variable_calculee.but: Adds a variable computed by an R formula on the project's variables and identifiers (Edit › New variable).

nom.description: The new variable's name; the spaces around it are dropped.

formule.description: An R expression, evaluated by R (it can call any R function) with each variable and each observation identifier under its name (a name with spaces or signs between `backticks`; a qualitative variable as its categories' names, one value per observation), and Nuée's helpers: moyenne_groupe/group_mean, ecart_groupe/group_deviation, precedent/previous, suivant/following, croissance/growth_rate, richesse/richness, shannon, simpson and pielou (variables.R). It must give one value per observation, or a single value for all: numbers make a quantitative variable (non-finite ones missing), text or logical values a qualitative one, its categories sorted.

resultat.description: The project with the new variable.

erreurs.message: Variable not found: <name> (check the name; a name with spaces or signs is written between `backticks`)
erreurs.quand: The formula names an object R doesn't find.

erreurs.message: The formula must give one value per observation (<n>); it gives <k>
erreurs.quand: The formula's result is neither one value nor one per observation.

erreurs.message: The formula must give numbers or text
erreurs.quand: The result is neither numbers, text, logical values nor a factor.

erreurs.message: <R's message>
erreurs.quand: The formula fails as R evaluates it (a wrong argument, stop()…), or one of Nuée's helpers refuses its arguments (precedent(): two observations with the same time in a group…): its message, as it is.

variable_calculee.effet_detail: One undo step (variable <name>); the variable joins the project's dataset Variables ajoutées.

classes_valeurs.but: Adds a qualitative variable made of classes of a quantitative variable's values, cut at given limits or at its quantiles.

nom.description: The new variable's name; the spaces around it are dropped.

variable.description: The number of the quantitative variable to cut.

bornes.description: The limits: 10 and 20 make the classes ≤ 10, ]10 ; 20] and > 20 (each class closed on the right, the limits written to 4 significant digits). One of bornes and n is needed.

n.description: Without bornes: the number of classes of about equal counts, their limits at the quantiles (duplicate limits merged).

resultat.description: The project with the new variable.

erreurs.message: Choose a quantitative variable
erreurs.quand: The variable is qualitative.

erreurs.message: At least one limit is needed
erreurs.quand: bornes is empty, or n gives no limit inside the values (n = 1).

erreurs.message: non-numeric argument to binary operator
erreurs.quand: Neither bornes nor n is given: R then reads n from nom, whose name starts with it, and fails (R's own message).

imputer.but: Fills the missing values of quantitative variables by regularized iterative PCA, as missMDA::imputePCA does.

variables.description: The numbers of the quantitative variables, at least two: each one is filled from the others; the complete ones only help.

k.description: The number of components; without it, chosen from 0 to 5 by generalized cross-validation of the scaled variables, as missMDA::estim_ncpPCA (0: each variable's mean). A given k is kept at most min(p − 1, n − 2).

bornes.description: Keep each imputed value within its variable's observed range (a 0/1 variable between 0 and 1, an area positive).

remplacer.description: true fills the variables themselves; otherwise new variables "<name> (imputed)" ("(imputée)" in French) receive the values, updated when imputed again.

resultat.description: The project after the imputation.

imputation.description: {valeurs: the cells filled; tours: the iterations; composantes: the components used (0: the means); choisies: true when that number was chosen; laissees: the observations left missing, which lack more than half of the variables}.

erreurs.message: Imputation by PCA goes with quantitative variables.
erreurs.quand: One of the variables is qualitative.

erreurs.message: Choose at least two variables: the PCA fills each one from the others.
erreurs.quand: Fewer than two different variables.

erreurs.message: These variables have no missing values.
erreurs.quand: Nothing is missing in these variables.

erreurs.message: A constant or nearly empty variable can't be imputed: <names>.
erreurs.quand: A variable has no variation (or no values) over the observations that miss at most half of them.

erreurs.message: No value to fill: each incomplete observation misses more than half of these variables.
erreurs.quand: Every observation with a missing value lacks more than half of the variables.

erreurs.message: Too few observations for a PCA: at least 3 are needed that miss at most half of these variables.
erreurs.quand: Fewer than 3 observations miss at most half of the variables.

imputer.effet_detail: One undo step (imputation); the new variables are named in the request's language. The observed values don't change.

classe_selection.but: Puts observations in a category of a qualitative class variable, the variable and the category created if needed.

variable.description: The class variable's name, not its number: a new qualitative variable when no variable has it (a number is taken as a name).

etiquette.description: The category's name, added after the variable's others if it is new.

observations.description: The numbers of the observations to put in it; the others keep their category (or none).

resultat.description: The project after the change.

erreurs.message: The variable “<name>” already exists and isn't qualitative
erreurs.quand: A quantitative variable with values has that name.

erreurs.message: subscript out of bounds
erreurs.quand: One of the observations isn't the project's (R's own message).

classe_selection.effet_detail: One undo step, labelled in French whatever the language (classe <category>); a new variable joins the dataset Variables ajoutées.

scores_en_variables.but: Makes the scores of a fitted PCA or PLS variables of its project, for a hierarchical model that takes them as X.

modele.description: The fitted model's id: a PCA, PLS or OPLS (NIPALS components).

projet.description: The project with the score variables.

noms.description: Their names, as .usp files name them: $<model>.t<a>(<title>), $M1.t1(Overview)… (always an array).

modeles.description: The names of the project's model definitions that use these variables, to fit again (always an array).

scores_en_variables.effet_detail: One undo step, labelled in French whatever the language (scores de <model> en variables). Each score variable has values for the model's observations only; doing it again after refitting the model updates the same variables.

table_a_joindre.but: Reads a table whose columns are to be added to the project and gives its tables, its columns and the keys proposed, before ajouter_colonnes adds them (Edit › Add columns from a table).

chemin.description: The table's file, in any format File › Open reads, or a project (.nuee, .json, .usp: its data). Needed without texte.

texte.description: Pasted cells instead of a file (tab, semicolon or comma separated, two lines at least): kept in a file of the engine's temporary folder, whose path comes back as chemin.

table.description: The file's sheet or table; by default its first (a Variables codebook sheet set aside).

chemin.description: The file to give ajouter_colonnes: the one given, or the file holding the pasted cells.

nom.description: The file's name, or "pasted cells" in the request's language.

colle.description: Whether the table came from pasted cells.

tables.description: The file's tables when it has several (sheets, R objects, layers), else null.

table.description: The table read (null for a format without tables): give it back to ajouter_colonnes.

colonnes.description: Its columns as columns: nom, their names; nombres, whether each holds numbers; nom_ajoute, the name each would take in the project ("name (2)" for a name taken); always arrays.

cles.description: The key proposed, each {projet: the project's column, a Colonne; table: the table's column}: columns of the same name (capitals and spaces around aside), the combination whose keys are unique in the table where the most observations find theirs; empty without a common name.

erreurs.message: Table not found in the file: <table>
erreurs.quand: table isn't one of an R file's tables.

erreurs.message: The .usp file couldn't be converted: <the converter's output>
erreurs.quand: A .usp project the converter can't read.

erreurs.message: <the reader's message>
erreurs.quand: The file is missing or can't be read: the message of R or of the package that reads it, often untranslated.

table_a_joindre.effet_detail: Pasted cells are written to a file of the engine's temporary folder; the project doesn't change.

ajouter_colonnes.but: Adds columns of a table to the project's observations, each observation taking the values of the row that has its key (Edit › Add columns from a table).

chemin.description: The table's file, as table_a_joindre's chemin gives it (for pasted cells, the file that keeps them).

table.description: Its sheet or table, as table_a_joindre's table gives it; without it, the file's first (which may be a Variables codebook sheet).

cles_projet.description: The project's columns that make the key: variables by number, identifiers as "id:k".

cles_table.description: The table's columns that answer them, in the same order, read as written ("01" stays "01"). Keys compare as numbers when the project's column is a quantitative variable, else as text without the spaces around, capitals counting.

colonnes.description: The table's columns to add; by default all but the key's.

nom.description: The table's name in the undo label; by default the file's name.

resultat.description: The project with the new variables.

jointure.description: {colonnes: the table's columns added; noms: the names they took ("name (2)" for a name taken); n: the observations; trouvees: those that found their key; sans_correspondance: those without, their values missing; cles_seules: the table's keys that match no observation; sans_cle: the table's rows without a key, left out; phrases: what happened, in sentences}. A single column or sentence comes as a string, not an array.

erreurs.message: Each key column needs its column in the project and in the table
erreurs.quand: cles_table is empty, or cles_projet and cles_table don't have the same length.

erreurs.message: The table has no column “<name>”
erreurs.quand: A column of cles_table or colonnes isn't the table's.

erreurs.message: A column comes only once in the key
erreurs.quand: A column is twice in cles_projet or in cles_table.

erreurs.message: A key column isn't added to the project
erreurs.quand: colonnes names a column of the key.

erreurs.message: Choose at least one column to add
erreurs.quand: No column is left to add.

erreurs.message: The key “<key>”<columns> comes <n> times in the table<, as do <k> other(s)>: each key must come at most once (add to the key the column that tells these rows apart, the year for instance)
erreurs.quand: A key is on several rows of the table.

erreurs.message: No observation finds its key<columns> in the table: nothing was added. Keys are compared as written (S1 isn't s1, nor 01 1); the project has <keys>, the table <keys>.
erreurs.quand: No observation's key is in the table.

erreurs.message: <the reader's message>
erreurs.quand: The file is missing or can't be read: the message of R or of the package that reads it, often untranslated.

ajouter_colonnes.effet_detail: One undo step (columns from <nom>); numbers make quantitative variables, the rest qualitative ones; the models already fitted don't change.

raster_infos.but: Says what each raster file is and how many observations fall inside it, or why it can't be read, before ajouter_raster adds its values.

projet.description: The project's id; its coordinates must be set.

chemins.description: The raster files' paths: GeoTIFF (.tif) or ESRI ASCII grids (.asc).

fichiers.description: One per path, in their order (always an array). A file read: {chemin, nom, taille (bytes), format (GeoTIFF, BigTIFF or ASCII), largeur, hauteur (cells), bandes, type (uint8, int16, float32…, texte_entiers or texte for an ASCII grid), compression ("" without), predicteur, organisation (tiles or strips, in words), bandes_separees, resolution (the cells' size, in words), etendue {xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax} in its system, systeme {code (null when unknown), nom, suppose: taken as the project's for want of its own}, nodata (null without), palette, pixel_point, methode (the method proposed: cellule for classes, bilineaire otherwise), noms (each band's proposed name), noms_libres (the names they would take in the project), dedans (the observations inside), observations (those with coordinates), total, notes (always arrays for noms, noms_libres and notes)}. A file that can't be read: {chemin, nom, taille (null when missing), erreur: why, in the request's language}.

raster_infos.effet_detail: A file that can't be read doesn't fail the request: its entry says why in erreur.

ajouter_raster.but: Adds the values of raster files at the observations' coordinates as new variables, one per band (Edit › Add raster values).

projet.description: The project's id; its coordinates must be set.

fichiers.description: The files, each {chemin: its path; methode: how a value is read, cellule (the cell holding the observation), bilineaire (interpolated from the four nearest cells), moyenne or majorite (the mean, or the majority class, of the cells within rayon), another or none being the method raster_infos proposes; rayon: the circle's radius in metres, for moyenne and majorite, at most 50000; noms: one name per band, by default the names raster_infos proposes}. Bands of different files given the same name make one variable, as tiles of one raster: they must then share their method and radius.

resultat.description: The project with the new variables.

raster.description: {variables: one per variable added (always an array), each {nom: its name ("name (2)" for a name taken), demande: the name asked, fichiers (always an array), methode, rayon (null without), valeurs: the observations with a value, sans_coordonnees, hors: outside the raster, sans_valeur: on a cell without a value, note: the files' notes, null, one string or several}; phrases: what happened, in sentences, one alone coming as a string}.

erreurs.message: Choose at least one raster file.
erreurs.quand: fichiers is empty.

erreurs.message: No observation has coordinates.
erreurs.quand: Every observation lacks a coordinate.

erreurs.message: File not found: <path>
erreurs.quand: A file doesn't exist.

erreurs.message: <file>: Nuée reads GeoTIFF rasters (.tif) and ESRI ASCII grids (.asc). For another format, export it as GeoTIFF in QGIS (right-click on the layer › Export › Save As…).
erreurs.quand: A file is neither.

erreurs.message: <file>: give the circle's radius, in metres.
erreurs.quand: methode is moyenne or majorite without a positive rayon.

erreurs.message: <file>: a radius over 50 km isn't computed here.
erreurs.quand: rayon is over 50000.

erreurs.message: <file> has <n> band(s): give each one a name.
erreurs.quand: noms doesn't give one name per band.

erreurs.message: <file>: give each band a name.
erreurs.quand: A band's name is empty.

erreurs.message: The files joined under the name “<name>” must have the same method and radius.
erreurs.quand: Bands given the same name have different methods or radii.

erreurs.message: <file> is in <system>, and the project's coordinates are plane, without a stated system: choose their system in Plots › Map.
erreurs.quand: The raster has a system and the project's coordinates are "plan".

erreurs.message: <file> : <why the file is refused>
erreurs.quand: The file can't be read (damaged, a compression or a value type Nuée doesn't read, a coordinate system it doesn't convert…): raster.R's refusals, each naming the file.

ajouter_raster.effet_detail: One undo step (values from <files>); each variable keeps where it came from (its files, bands, method, radius, system and cell size), which the Methods text says.

resumer_groupes.but: Summarizes a project into a new project of one observation per group of one or more columns (Edit › Summarize by group).

projet.description: The project to summarize, which doesn't change.

groupes.description: The columns that make the groups (the sector and the year…): variables by number, identifiers as "id:k". An observation without a value in one of them is left out, and counted.

variables.description: The quantitative variables to summarize; by default all of them but those of the groups.

statistiques.description: One or more statistics, each for every variable, in columns "<variable> (<statistic>)" named in the request's language; missing values are ignored.

valeurs.ecart_type: The standard deviation (missing for a single value).

resultat.description: The new project, named "<project> by <groups>" in the request's language: its observations the groups, named by their values, in the order of their columns; the group columns as they were (variables or identifiers); the qualitative variables and identifiers that don't vary within any group; the summaries.

resume.description: {groupes: the number of groups; observations: those summarized; sans_groupe: those left out for a missing group value; gardees: the qualitative variables and identifiers kept; laissees: those left out, as they vary within a group; phrase: that in a sentence}. One name alone in gardees or laissees comes as a string.

erreurs.message: Choose at least one column to make the groups
erreurs.quand: groupes is empty.

erreurs.message: Choose at least one statistic
erreurs.quand: statistiques is empty.

erreurs.message: Unknown statistic: <name>
erreurs.quand: A statistic isn't one of the values.

erreurs.message: “<name>” is qualitative: only quantitative variables are summarized (a qualitative variable is kept when it doesn't vary within a group)
erreurs.quand: variables names a qualitative variable.

erreurs.message: Choose at least one quantitative variable to summarize
erreurs.quand: No quantitative variable is left outside the groups.

erreurs.message: No observation has a value of <columns>
erreurs.quand: No observation has a value in every group column.

resumer_groupes.effet_detail: Opens the new project in the session, without a file and marked modified; the project summarized doesn't change.

remplacer.but: Finds and replaces values in one, several or all variables, or previews what the replacement would change (Edit › Find and replace).

variables.description: The numbers of the variables to search; all of them without it.

chercher.description: The text or number to find; needed unless vides. A qualitative variable compares it as text (the whole cell, without the spaces around, or with partie a part of it); a quantitative one as a number on the whole cell ("3,5" is 3.5).

remplacer.description: What replaces it; empty, the cells become empty (missing). A quantitative variable takes only a number or nothing: with a text, its cells stay as they are, and are counted (ignorees).

vides.description: Find the empty cells (missing values) instead; chercher is then ignored.
