partie.description: In a qualitative variable, replace chercher wherever it appears in the text ("," in "3,5"), as written; not with vides.

nombres.description: A qualitative variable whose values, once replaced, are all numbers becomes quantitative.

apercu.description: Only say what would change, changing nothing.

resultat.description: With apercu, an object with remplacement only; otherwise the project after the change, with remplacement.

remplacement.description: {cellules: the cells changed; variables: one per variable searched (always an array), each {variable, nom, cellules, ignorees: the cells left (a text for a quantitative variable), devient: quantitative, qualitative or "" when it stays what it was, categories_avant, categories_apres, exemples: the first changes, "a → b (n)", one alone as a string}; phrases: what changes, in sentences, one alone as a string}.

erreurs.message: Give the text or number to find, or find the empty cells.
erreurs.quand: chercher is empty without vides.

erreurs.message: No variable to search.
erreurs.quand: The project has no variable with data.

erreurs.message: No cell to replace.
erreurs.quand: Without apercu, no cell would change.

remplacer.effet_detail: With apercu nothing changes. Otherwise one undo step (replacement of <text>, or of empty cells); a category replaced by an existing one merges into it, one emptied disappears, and the project's model definitions follow the categories (atelier.R: suivre_categories).

categories.but: Renames, merges or reorders the categories of a qualitative variable (Edit › Categories).

noms.description: The new name of each of its categories, in their present order (Projet's categories): two given the same name merge into one. No name may be empty.

ordre.description: The order of the categories that result, by their names, each once; by default the order they come in (a merge takes the place of the first). In a regression, the last category observed is the reference.

resultat.description: The project after the change.

categories.description: {variable, nom, categories: the categories now (always an array), reference: the last, a regression's reference, phrases: what changed, in sentences}.

erreurs.message: <name> is quantitative: it has no categories.
erreurs.quand: The variable is quantitative.

erreurs.message: Give a name to each of the <n> categories of <name>.
erreurs.quand: noms doesn't give one name per category.

erreurs.message: A category can't have an empty name (Edit › Find and replace empties cells).
erreurs.quand: A name is empty.

erreurs.message: The order must give each category once: <categories>.
erreurs.quand: ordre doesn't give each resulting category once.

erreurs.message: The categories didn't change.
erreurs.quand: The names and order are those of now.

categories.effet_detail: One undo step (categories of <name>); the observations keep their category under its new name, the project's model definitions follow, and a model of the session fitted with a category since renamed or merged must be fitted again before it refits or predicts (modele_perime).

decrire_variables.but: Sets the unit and the description of variables (Edit › Units and descriptions).

descriptions.description: One per variable, {variable: its number; unite: its unit, cut to 60 characters; description: cut to 1000}: a field absent or null stays as it is, an empty text removes it; line breaks and other control characters become spaces.

resultat.description: The project after the change (Projet's variables carry unite and description).

erreurs.message: No variable to describe.
erreurs.quand: descriptions is empty.

erreurs.message: The units and descriptions didn't change.
erreurs.quand: Every value given is the one already there.

coordonnees.but: Gives the project's coordinates, a proposal made from its variables' names and the coordinate systems offered, and with regler sets or removes them.

regler.description: true sets the coordinates to x, y and systeme, or removes them without x.

x.description: With regler: the number of the variable holding x (the east, or the longitude); absent, the coordinates are removed.

y.description: With regler and x: the number of the variable holding y (the north, or the latitude).

systeme.description: With regler and x: their system, an EPSG code (2154, or "EPSG:2154") among those Nuée knows (WGS 84, ETRS89, RGF93, Lambert-93, CC42 to CC50, Lambert II étendu, LAEA Europe, web Mercator, UTM zones), or "plan" for plane coordinates in metres of an unstated system.

coordonnees.description: The coordinates set (after the change, with regler); null without.

proposition.description: Two quantitative variables whose names look like coordinates (longitude and latitude, X and Y, east and north…), {x, y, systeme: the system their values suggest, 4326, 2154, 27572 or "plan"}; null when none do.

systemes.description: The systems the interface lists, each {code, nom} (always an array).

projet.description: With regler, the project after the change; null otherwise.

erreurs.message: Unknown coordinate system: <code>
erreurs.quand: With regler, systeme isn't a system Nuée knows.

erreurs.message: Coordinates must be two different quantitative variables of the project.
erreurs.quand: With regler, x or y isn't a quantitative variable of the project, or they are the same.

erreurs.message: Longitudes and latitudes run from −180 to 180 and from −90 to 90: “<x>” or “<y>” goes beyond. Choose the system of the plane coordinates.
erreurs.quand: With regler, a longitude and latitude system for values beyond those bounds.

coordonnees.effet_detail: Only with regler: true, which sets the coordinates (or removes them) as one undo step (coordinates); without it nothing changes.

verifier.but: Checks a model's data before it is fitted: the variables and observations with more than half of their values missing, and the constant variables.

resultat.description: Only the problems; TRIM and DISTANCE check their own data when fitted, and give two empty tables written {}.

variables.description: A table of the variables that have more than half of their values missing or are constant: uid, nom, manquantes (the share missing, from 0 to 1, of its worst term), constante; its columns are empty arrays when there is none.

observations.description: A table of the observations that miss more than half of their X values: uid, nom, manquantes (a share, from 0 to 1).

erreurs.message: An OPLS needs at least one Y variable
erreurs.quand: An OPLS without y.

erreurs.message: Unknown spectral preprocessing: <type>
erreurs.quand: A step of spectres isn't snv, msc, sg, detrend or ligne_base.

erreurs.message: Cross-validation: this project has no ID "<id>".
erreurs.quand: vc names an identifier the project hasn't.

erreurs.message: Unknown grouping "<by>"
erreurs.quand: A random effect's or the CAR1 time's by is neither id nor variable.

condition_observations.but: Counts the ticked observations that a model's condition keeps, for New model's Observations tab.

condition.description: The condition, an R expression read without running anything (condition.R: lire_condition); empty or absent, every ticked observation counts.

exclues.description: The unticked observations' numbers, not counted.

test.description: The test set's observations, not counted either.

n.description: The ticked observations where the condition is true (a missing value counts as false).

noms_x.description: The X terms, in the order of p's arrays (always an array).

noms_y.description: The Y terms, in the order of c's arrays (always an array, empty for a PCA).

ipls.but: Fits interval PLS models on consecutive ranges of a model's spectrum and gives each range's RMSEcv for 1 to A components (iPLS, Nørgaard et al. 2000).

modele.description: The fitted model's id: a PLS, PLS-DA or OPLS whose quantitative X make a spectrum (an OPLS is fitted as a PLS).

n.description: The number of intervals of about the same width, at most the number of spectrum variables (brought back within that range).

A.description: Up to how many components each interval's PLS is fitted with; the model's A by default.

intervalles.description: One per interval, in the spectrum's order: {termes, variables (its terms and their variables' numbers), rmsecv (for 1, 2… A components, null where even one component doesn't fit), A (the number that gives the smallest RMSEcv, null if none)}; the arrays always arrays.

complet.description: The same for the whole spectrum, {rmsecv, A}: it gives the model back.

A.description: The largest number of components tried.

spectre.description: The spectrum's terms, in order (always an array).

moyen.description: The mean preprocessed spectrum, one value per term of spectre (always an array).

autres.description: The model's other X terms (qualitative ones, cross terms), in every interval's model (always an array).

effets.but: Gives the effect of each quantitative term of a regression along its variable's values, on the link's scale with its 95 % band, one per category for a term crossed with categories.

lien.description: The model's link: identity, log, logit…

effets.description: One per quantitative term, main effects first, then the terms that only enter through a cross term with categories. A term alone: {terme, courbe (a smooth curve, else a straight line), x (80 values over the variable's range, in its units, transformed if it is), effet (centred on the variable's mean, the other terms fixed), bas, haut (the 95 % band), valeurs (the observed values)}. A term crossed with categories: {terme, courbe, par (their variables, "a × b"), valeurs, niveaux: one {niveau, x, effet, bas, haut, valeurs, and for a straight line pente, pente_bas, pente_haut per unit of the variable} per category observed}. A curve per category: {terme, courbe: true, par_categorie: true, par, valeurs, niveaux: one {niveau, x, effet, bas, haut, valeurs} per category}.

effets.effet_detail: Computed once and kept with the fitted model: later calls give the kept result.

seuils.but: Gives a GAM curve's effect and slope with simultaneous 95 % bands, and the ranges where the slope is clearly positive or negative, as thresholds (Simpson 2018).

modele.description: The fitted regression's id: a GAM, or a model with a curve fitted by mgcv.

terme.description: The curve's term, by its name as in the model's coefficients and curves.

categorie.description: For a curve per category (s(x, by = f)) or a curve crossed with categories: the category whose curve to read; the first without it.
Only for a curve with categories: the category read.

par.description: Only for a curve with categories: its qualitative variable or variables ("a × b").

edf.description: The curve's effective degrees of freedom.

p.description: The p of the curve's test (mgcv).

lineaire.description: edf below 1.5: the curve is almost a straight line.

amplitude.description: The range of the effect over the grid.

x.description: 200 values from the 2nd to the 98th percentile of the variable (in that category), in the variable's units.

effet.description: The curve at x, on the link's scale, centred on its mean.

bas.description: The lower edge of its simultaneous 95 % band (2000 draws of the coefficients, a fixed seed).

haut.description: The upper edge of that band.

x_pente.description: The 199 midpoints between consecutive values of x.

pente.description: The curve's slope at x_pente, per unit of the variable.

pente_bas.description: The lower edge of the slope's simultaneous 95 % band.

sens.description: At each midpoint: "hausse" (the band of the slope is above 0), "baisse" (below 0) or "ns".

plages_pente.description: A table (columns) of the ranges where the slope is clearly positive or negative: sens ("hausse" or "baisse"), de, a (from, to).

plages_effet.description: A table (columns) of the ranges where the effect is clearly above or below its mean: sens ("au_dessus" or "au_dessous"), de, a.

critique_effet.description: The critical multiplier of the effect's simultaneous band.

tirages.description: The number of draws of the coefficients, 2000.

valeurs.description: The variable's observed values (in that category), in its units: a rug.

erreurs.message: Thresholds are read on a curve of an additive model.
erreurs.quand: The regression wasn't fitted by mgcv: an LM, or an LMM fitted by nlme.

apports.but: Gives what each group of terms brings to a regression, from the model refitted by maximum likelihood without it: the change of AIC and the likelihood-ratio test.

apports.description: A table (columns), one row per group of terms (its block in New model, else its variable): groupe, termes (how many terms leave with it), delta_aic (the AIC without it minus the full model's, both ML: above 0 the group improves the model, above 2 clearly), khi2, ddl, p (the likelihood-ratio test; null when the refit fails), avec (the groups that leave with it, the cross terms that need it, comma-separated). An empty object {} for a model without terms.

apports.effet_detail: Computed once and kept with the fitted model: later calls give the kept result.

selection_aic.but: Selects a regression's fixed effects by AICc over every allowed combination of its groups of terms, or by backward elimination beyond 256 combinations, each candidate refitted by maximum likelihood.

modele.description: The fitted regression's id. Its random effects, autocorrelation, distribution, offset and curves' settings stay those of the model; a cross term enters only with its main effects; the groups that carry a random slope stay in every candidate.

K.description: The number of groups chosen among. With 0, the result has only K, N and gardes.

N.description: The model's number of observations, those of every candidate.

gardes.description: The groups kept in every candidate: those carrying a random slope and those they need (always an array).

methode.description: "toutes" (every combination, 2^K at most limite) or "descendante" (backward elimination: at each step, the removal that lowers AICc the most).

limite.description: The most combinations fitted all together, 256.

groupes.description: The groups chosen among, by name (always an array).

termes.description: Each group's terms, in the order of groupes.

requis.description: The groups each group needs (a cross term, its main effects), in the order of groupes.

modeles.description: A table (columns) of the candidates, by increasing AICc (failed fits last): modele (its groups, "a + b", "1" for the null model), n_groupes, k (parameters), logLik, AICc, delta (ΔAICc), poids (Akaike weight), poids_cumule, etape (the step of the backward elimination, null for every combination).

contient.description: For each group, in the order of groupes: 1 or 0 for each row of modeles, whether it contains that group.

importance.description: A table (columns): groupe, importance (the sum of the weights of the candidates that contain it).

meilleur.description: The row of modeles of the best candidate, the lowest AICc: 1.

parcimonieux.description: The row of the most parsimonious candidate: the fewest parameters among those with ΔAICc at most 2.

chemin.description: The backward elimination's steps, a table (columns) etape, retire (the group removed), AICc; null for every combination.

echecs.description: The number of candidates whose fit failed.

erreurs.message: No model has an AICc: too few observations for their parameters.
erreurs.quand: Every candidate's fit failed or has no AICc.

selection_aic.effet_detail: Computed once and kept with the fitted model: methodes then describes the selection and script_r redoes it.

autocorrelation_residus.but: Gives the autocorrelation of a regression's residuals along time within groups, pooled as nlme's ACF, to see whether a CAR1 autocorrelation is needed or is enough.

modele.description: The fitted regression's id. A model with CAR1 uses its own time and groups, and the next two parameters are ignored.

temps.description: The time, an identifier ({by: "id", id}) or a variable ({by: "variable", variable}), numbers or dates; required without CAR1. Several: the first.

groupe.description: The groups within which the residuals follow each other, nested from the widest to the finest; {by: "effets"} stands for the model's random effects. Without it, all the observations make one series.

valeurs.deviance: Each observation's signed part of the deviance

type.description: The residuals of a model fitted by mgcv alone (a GLM, a GAM); the others' are Pearson's.

phi.description: Its CAR1 φ, null without CAR1.

groupe.description: The groups' names, "site / sector"; null for one series.

laissees.description: The model's observations left out, without a time or a group.

decalage.description: The lags, 0 to min(10, the longest series minus 1): successive observations of a series, not units of time.

paires.description: The pairs of observations at each lag.

bande.description: ±1.96/√pairs at each lag: the band of nlme's plot.

series.description: {residus, acf (one value per lag)}: the residuals (residus "pearson" or "deviance"), and with CAR1 a second series of its normalized residuals ("normalises"), which show no autocorrelation left when CAR1 accounts for it.

rapports_vraisemblance.but: Gives the likelihood-ratio tests between the nested pairs among some regressions that differ only by their fixed effects, as anova(m1, m2) on their maximum-likelihood fits.

Two are compared when they have the same response, observations, distribution, effort, random effects (slopes included) and autocorrelation, and one's fixed terms lie within the other's.

paires.description: A table (columns), one row per nested pair: grand, petit (the bigger and the smaller model's ids), ddl, khi2 (2 × the difference of their ML log-likelihoods, 0 at least), p, approche (true when one has curves or mgcv random effects: edf, an approximate test). An empty object {} without any pair.

total.description: The number of nested pairs found.

max.description: At most that many pairs are given, 2000.

coefficients_modeles.but: Puts several regressions' coefficients side by side with their fit statistics, as the cells of a table for an article.

modeles.description: The fitted regressions' ids, in the order of the columns.

erreur.description: What follows each estimate; any other value is ic.

modeles.description: The columns' names: the models' names, made unique with a number (always an array).

entete.description: The header of the terms' column ("Estimate [95% CI]", "Estimate (SE)").

termes.description: The rows: the first model's terms, then the next ones' that it hasn't (always an array).

cellules.description: One row per term, one cell per model: the estimate with its interval or standard error, as text with the decimal mark of the request's language; "" when the model hasn't the term.

p.description: Each cell's p, null where the model hasn't the term.

statistiques.description: The fit rows that some model has: n, AIC, AICc, R², marginal and conditional R², deviance explained, the distribution's parameters, σ of each random effect and of the residual, ρ of random slopes, φ (CAR1), each curve's edf (always an array).

valeurs.description: One row per fit statistic, one cell per model, as text.

note_lien.description: What the estimates mean for a model with a log or logit link; null when every link is the identity.

copie.description: The same table for the clipboard: {entetes (always an array), lignes (rows of text: the terms with their cells, the p's stars added, then the fit rows), notes (the stars' legend and the link's note, always an array)}.

puissance_tendance.but: Computes the power of monitoring designs to detect a trend with a linear regression or a linear mixed model's variances, and on request checks one design by simulation.

modele.description: The fitted regression's id: an LM, or an LMM fitted by nlme (with or without CAR1), with random intercepts only and a quantitative untransformed X for the time. Without any other parameter, the result of the last computation for this model (its sentence in the request's language), else the defaults.

terme.description: The time: the name of a quantitative, untransformed X term of the model. By default the first whose name looks like a time (year, date, time, season, année…), else the CAR1 time's variable, else the first such term.

valeurs.pente: A slope in the response's units per unit of time
valeurs.pourcent: A change in % per year, for a response in log10 or ln

unite.description: The trend's unit; pourcent by default for a response in log10 or ln, else pente (any other value: the default).

tendance.description: The trend to detect, not 0; by default -3 (% per year), or in pente minus 3 % of the mean response's absolute value, rounded to 2 significant digits.

alpha.description: The level of the two-sided test.

annees.description: The first and last numbers of years of the curves, whole numbers from 3 to 100; by default 5 to the data's span or 30, whichever is larger, 100 at most (another number of values than two: the default).

unites.description: The numbers of units (the first random effect's, or observations per year for an LM) of the curves, whole numbers from 2 (1 for an LM) to 10000; the data's own number is always added, 10 numbers at most. By default the data's number times 0.5, 1, 1.5 and 2.

simulation.description: The simulation's design, {annees (3 to 100, by default the data's span), unites (by default the data's), n (data sets, 10 to 2000, by default 200)}; its expected duration is in estimation.

simuler.description: true to run the simulation now, unless one with the same settings is kept; refused beyond 20000 observations per data set or about 15 minutes.

reglages.description: The settings used: {terme, unite, tendance, alpha, annees ([first, last], always an array), unites (always an array), simulation {annees, unites, n}}.

termes.description: The X terms that can be the time (always an array).

pourcent_possible.description: Whether the response is in log10 or ln, so a trend in % can be given.

approchee.description: A trend in % on log(a·y + c) with c not 0: an approximation.

transformation.description: The response's transformation, as text ("" without one).

forme.description: That transformation as the definition keeps it; null without one.

pente.description: The slope to detect on the response's scale, per unit of time.

pente_modele.description: The model's own slope of the time, in its units, for comparison.

y_modele.description: The response as written with its transformation.

niveaux.description: The random effects' levels, from the widest (always an array, empty for an LM).

dans.description: The finer group within which CAR1 runs, if any.

temps_car1.description: The CAR1 time's name, if any.

croises.description: The model's cross terms with the time, left out of the designs (always an array).

plan.description: The data's design: {annees (years spanned), N, unites, emboites and moyennes (nested units per level, rounded and mean; always arrays), dans, moyenne_dans (CAR1 groups in the finest unit), repetitions, moyenne_repetitions (observations per series and year), series_par_unite}.

variances.description: The model's REML variances: {sigma2 (residual), niveaux (each random effect's; always an array), phi (CAR1's φ, null without CAR1)}.

tableau.description: A table (columns), one row per design: annees, unites, observations, erreur_type (of the GLS slope), puissance.

seuil.description: 0.8, the power that annees_80 looks for.

annees_80.description: A table (columns): unites, annees (the fewest years for 80 % power, null when the curves don't reach it).

simulation.description: The simulation once run with these settings, else null: {annees, unites, n, graine, alpha, observations, puissance (the share of p at most alpha), erreur_mc (its Monte Carlo error), echecs, duree (seconds), p (each data set's p), cle (the settings it was run with), analytique (the formula's power at that design)}.

facteur.description: The qualitative X variable whose categories' means are computed, by its number; the model's first qualitative variable by default.

dans.description: A qualitative variable crossed with facteur in a term of the model, by its number: facteur's categories are compared within each of its categories (simple effects).

pente.description: A quantitative variable crossed with facteur in a term, by its number: its slope in each category instead of the means (as emtrends).

forme_y.description: The response as written with its transformation, null without one.

verifications_modele.but: Checks a regression's conditions after its fit and says each in words: the residuals' distribution and spread, influential observations, overdispersion, zeros, collinearity, concurvity and spatial autocorrelation.

modele.description: The fitted model's id; for a model that isn't a regression, the list is empty.

verifications.description: One per condition checked, {cle, statut, texte}: cle "loi" (Shapiro–Wilk on the standardized or quantile residuals), "variance" (Spearman between the residuals' size and the fitted values), "influence" (Cook's distance beyond 4/n, an LM), "dispersion" (Poisson), "zeros" (zeros observed against expected), "colinearite" (VIF), "concurvite" (curves), "spatial" (Moran's I of the residuals, a project with coordinates and 3000 observations at most); statut "ok", "attention" or "info"; texte, what was seen and what to do, in the request's language (X-Langue).

verifications_modele.effet_detail: Computed once per language and kept with the fitted model.

resultats_texte.but: Writes a model's Results text, what it shows in sentences with its numbers, in French or in English.

langue.description: The text's language; any other value, or none, is French (this request doesn't follow X-Langue).

paragraphes.description: The paragraphs. A regression: its fit (R², marginal and conditional R², deviance explained, Q², AIC), each coefficient with its interval and p (a factor or an odds ratio for a log or logit link), the significant terms, its curves and random effects. A PCA, PLS or OPLS: R²X, R²Y and Q² by component, the gain over the empty model, CV-ANOVA, the variables with VIP above 1. Another analysis: its own text, or its summary figures.

methodes.but: Writes a model's Methods text for an article, with its references, in French or in English.

modele.description: The fitted model's id. What was computed and kept with it (the AIC selection, the trend power, the adjusted means) is described too.

langue.description: The text's language; any other value, or none, is French (this request doesn't follow X-Langue).

version.description: Nuée's version, written in the text and in its reference to Nuée; "" leaves it out.

paragraphes.description: The paragraphs: the data, their preprocessing, the method, its validation, the model's quality, the software.

references.description: The references the text cites, in APA style, sorted.

arbre_stabilite.but: Gives how stable a decision tree's first split is over bootstrap draws of its groups, computed once and kept with the model.

modele.description: A decision tree (TREE) fitted in the session.

stabilite.description: A table, as columns, one row per variable that made the first split of a draw's tree, the most frequent first: variable ("(no split)" for trees without a split, in the request's language), tirages, frequence (in %), seuil_median (its median threshold).

tirages.description: The number of draws: the model's setting tirages (200 by default).

echecs.description: The draws whose tree couldn't be grown.

erreurs.message: Only for a decision tree.
erreurs.quand: modele isn't a decision tree (TREE).

arbre_stabilite.effet_detail: Computed at the first request (the groups drawn with replacement, a fixed seed, 2026; each tree grown and pruned again) and kept with the session's model: later requests give it back.

dependance_partielle.but: Computes the partial dependence of the variables of a random forest or of boosted trees, keeps it with the model and gives it.

modele.description: A random forest (FOREST) or boosted trees (BOOST) fitted in the session.

variables.description: The names of the model's X variables wanted (their names, not their numbers); every one by default.

dependance.description: One per variable asked, in the order of the model's X (not of variables), each {variable, qualitative, x, tapis, and y, reponse or probabilites}: x, the grid (always an array: the variable's distinct values when at most 25, else 25 values evenly spaced from its minimum to its maximum; a qualitative variable's observed categories); tapis, the rug (always an array: its distinct values, or 300 quantiles beyond 300, or each category's count); y, the mean prediction at each value of the grid (a forest's response, or boosted trees' f on the link's scale); reponse, boosted trees' y on the response's scale; probabilites, a classification forest's mean share of votes, a table with a column per class.

erreurs.message: Only for a random forest or boosted trees.
erreurs.quand: modele is neither a FOREST nor a BOOST.

erreurs.message: Variable unknown to the model: <names>.
erreurs.quand: variables names a variable that isn't one of the model's X.

dependance_partielle.effet_detail: The dependences computed (those of earlier requests kept) stay with the session's model, and the names of their variables go into the model's definition in the project, saved with it and computed again when it opens: the project is marked modified when that list changes.

kmeans_choix.but: Gives, to choose k, the within-cluster sum of squares, R² and mean silhouette of the same k-means for k from 2 to 10, computed once and kept with the model.

modele.description: A k-means model (KMEANS) fitted in the session.

choix.description: A table, as columns, one row per k from 2 to 10 (fewer with few distinct observations): k, intra (the within-cluster sum of squares), r2 (between over total), silhouette (the mean silhouette; null beyond 3,000 observations).

kmeans_choix.effet_detail: Computed at the first request (the model's data and seed) and kept with the session's model: later requests give it back.

kmeans_variable.but: Adds the clusters of a k-means model to its project as a qualitative variable whose categories are 1 to k.

modele.description: A k-means model (KMEANS) fitted in the session; the variable goes to its project.

nom.description: The variable's name, trimmed; by default the model's name and "clusters" ("groupes" in French).

resultat.description: The model's project, with the variable.

erreurs.message: The variable “<name>” already exists and isn't qualitative
erreurs.quand: A quantitative variable with values has that name.

kmeans_variable.effet_detail: One undo step, labelled variable <name>. The variable holds the cluster of each of the model's observations, the others missing; a qualitative variable of that name already in the project is replaced (emptied, then given the clusters and the categories 1 to k).

rda_tests.but: Gives the permutation tests of an RDA's or a CCA's axes and terms (for a CCA, also its terms one after another), computed once and kept with the model.

modele.description: An RDA or a CCA fitted in the session with permutations.

axes.description: The constrained axes tested one after another (anova.cca by = "axis"), a table as columns: axe, ddl, inertie, F, p; p never decreases from one axis to the next, null for the axes after one at p = 1; the last row is the residual (labelled in the request's language).

termes.description: Each term tested after all the others (by = "margin"), except those a cross term contains, a table as columns: terme, ddl, inertie, F, p; the last row is the residual.

sequentiels.description: A CCA: its terms one after another in the model's order (by = "terms"), the same columns, the residual last; null for an RDA.

rda_tests.effet_detail: Computed at the first request with the model's permutations and kept with the session's model (and its exports): later requests give them back.

rda_selection.but: Gives the forward selection of an RDA's or a CCA's terms by adjusted R² and permutation tests (ordiR2step's double criterion), computed once and kept with the model.

modele.description: An RDA or a CCA fitted in the session with permutations.

etapes.description: The steps, a table as columns: terme (the candidate with the largest adjusted R²), r2_ajuste, F, p (its test against the model without it), retenu (whether it entered); null when no step was made.

retenus.description: The terms retained, in the order they entered (always an array).

r2_ajuste_tous.description: The adjusted R² of all the terms.

arret.description: Why the selection stopped: "tous" (no candidate left), "r2" (the best candidate doesn't increase the adjusted R²), "r2_tous" (it would exceed that of all the terms) or "p" (its p is above seuil).

erreurs.message: No selection: the adjusted R² of all the terms doesn't exist (too many terms for the observations).
erreurs.quand: The model's adjusted R² is missing.

rda_selection.effet_detail: Computed at the first request with the model's permutations and kept with the session's model (and its exports): later requests give it back.

rda_partition.but: Gives the partitioning of an RDA's variation between two or three sets of X variables, the blocks of its Variables tab, computed once and kept with the model.

modele.description: An RDA fitted in the session, without covariates Z, its X in two or three blocks (the terms without a block making one).

ensembles.description: A table, as columns, of each set and each union of sets (vegan's varpart): ensemble ("A + B"…), ddl, R2, r2_ajuste.

fractions.description: A table, as columns: fraction ([a], [b]…), sens (what it is, "A | B", "A ∩ B" or the residuals, in the request's language), r2_ajuste.

erreurs.message: Variation partitioning is done for an RDA, not for a CCA.
erreurs.quand: modele is a CCA.

erreurs.message: Variance partitioning is done without covariates Z.
erreurs.quand: The RDA has covariates Z.

erreurs.message: Variance partitioning needs two or three sets of X variables: give them a block (Block column of the Variables tab).
erreurs.quand: The X variables make one set, or more than three.

rda_partition.effet_detail: Computed at the first request and kept with the session's model (and its exports): later requests give it back.

statistiques_variables.but: Gives the descriptive statistics of each variable of a project, with the log transformation it suggests for a variable skewed to the right.

resultat.description: A table, as columns: one row per variable with data, in the project's order (diagnostic.R: statistiques_variables); every statistic is null for a qualitative variable. null for a project without variables.

nom.description: Its name.

categories.description: Its number of categories (0 for a quantitative variable).

manquantes.description: Its missing values, in % of the observations.

ecart_type.description: Its standard deviation (null with one value).

et_moyenne.description: Standard deviation / mean (null when the mean is 0).

asymetrie.description: Its skewness G1, corrected for the sample's size as Excel's (3 values and a variation at least).

test_asymetrie.description: The skewness over its standard error, √(6n(n − 1) / ((n − 2)(n + 1)(n + 3))).

aplatissement.description: Its excess kurtosis G2 (4 values at least).

rouge_min_max.description: 0 ≤ Min/Max < 0.1, which the interface shows in red.

rouge_asymetrie.description: |test_asymetrie| > 2, which the interface shows in red.

suggestion.description: The transformation suggested: "log10", or "log10:<C2>" for log10(x + C2), when the skewness is significant to the right (test_asymetrie > 2) and Min/Max without the zeros is under 0.1, with more than 4 values and more than 10 % of the observations; null otherwise.

C2.description: The constant of the suggestion: 0 when every value is positive, else half the smallest non-zero absolute value, plus that value when some are negative.

entiers.description: Whether every known value is a whole number (a count, a presence–absence); null for a qualitative variable.

zeros.description: The share of zeros among the known values, in %.

correlations_variables.but: Gives the correlation matrix of a project's quantitative variables, each pair on the observations where both are known, with its p-values corrected for multiple testing.

correction.description: The correction of the p-values over the K(K − 1)/2 pairs; any other value counts as BH.

valeurs.BH: Benjamini and Hochberg (1995), the false discovery rate.

uid.description: The numbers of the project's quantitative variables, in its order: the rows and columns of the matrices.

r.description: The correlations, a K × K matrix as an array of rows.

n.description: The number of observations of each pair.

p.description: Each pair's two-sided p-value (the t approximation, n − 2 degrees of freedom); null on the diagonal and for a pair of fewer than 3 observations.

p_ajuste.description: The p-values corrected over the pairs; null on the diagonal.

erreurs.message: Unknown method: <methode>
erreurs.quand: methode is neither pearson nor spearman.

erreurs.message: At least two quantitative variables are needed
erreurs.quand: The project has fewer than two quantitative variables with data.

erreurs.message: The correlation matrix is limited to 300 quantitative variables (this project has <K>): test them two at a time.
erreurs.quand: The project has more than 300 quantitative variables (spectra).

tests_variables.but: Compares every quantitative variable of a project between the classes of a qualitative variable, one test per variable, with the p-values corrected for multiple testing.

classe.description: The number of the qualitative variable whose classes are compared (a variable, not "id:k").

groupes.description: For a test of two classes: the classes A (the reference) and B, by their names; the first two categories by default. anova and kruskal compare every class and ignore it.

test.description: The test; t_apparie by default when appariement is given.

valeurs.mann_whitney: The Mann–Whitney test, two classes (on ranks).
valeurs.kruskal: The Kruskal–Wallis test, every class (on ranks).
valeurs.t_apparie: The paired t-test, two classes paired by appariement, on the differences B − A.
valeurs.wilcoxon: The Wilcoxon signed-rank test, two classes paired by appariement.

correction.description: The correction of the p-values over the variables; any other value counts as BH.

valeurs.BH: Benjamini and Hochberg (1995), the false discovery rate.

appariement.description: For a paired test: a variable or "id:k" (not "id:1") pairing the rows of A and B that have the same value (the year, for two sectors followed the same years), three pairs at least per variable. A paired test takes it, and it takes a paired test.

tableau.description: A table, as columns, one row per quantitative variable other than the class and the key: uid, nom, statistique, p and p_ajuste (p corrected over the variables); for two classes, n_a, n_b, moyenne_a, moyenne_b, log2_rapport (the log2 of B's mean over A's, when both are positive) and d (Cohen's d on the pooled standard deviation); for a paired test, n_paires, moyenne_a and moyenne_b on the pairs, log2_rapport and d (Cohen's d_z, the mean difference over the differences' standard deviation); for anova and kruskal, a column "moyenne <class>" per class. statistique and p are null for a variable that couldn't be tested (fewer than 2 values in a class, fewer than 3 pairs).

groupes.description: The classes compared: A and B, or every class.

effectifs.description: Each class's number of observations, by its name.

cle.description: With appariement: the key, {uid, nom, qualitative}.

erreurs.message: The class variable must be qualitative
erreurs.quand: classe is a quantitative variable.

erreurs.message: Two different classes are needed to compare
erreurs.quand: A test of two classes, and groupes doesn't name two different categories of the class.

erreurs.message: A paired test (paired t, Wilcoxon) takes a pairing key, and a pairing key a paired test
erreurs.quand: t_apparie or wilcoxon without appariement, or appariement with another test.

erreurs.message: The pairing key must be another variable than the class
erreurs.quand: appariement is the class variable.

erreurs.message: No quantitative variable to compare
erreurs.quand: The project has no quantitative variable besides the class and the key.

test_deux_variables.but: Tests two variables against each other with the tests their types call for, or with a paired test, checks the tests' conditions and says which one to read and why.

x.description: The first variable: a variable's number, or "id:k" (not "id:1"), which makes groups as a qualitative variable does.

y.description: The second variable, likewise; not x.

appariement.description: For a paired test: with a measurement and a qualitative variable, a third variable or "id:k" (not "id:1") pairing the rows of two of its levels that have the same value (the year, for two sectors); with two measurements, "observation": the same row holds both values (before and after).

niveaux.description: A paired test between levels: the two levels A and B compared, by name; the first two present by default.

dans.description: A paired test between levels: a fourth variable, qualitative, or "id:k" (not "id:1") making groups of levels (the site): the table of all the pairs keeps the pairs of levels of a same group.

resultat.description: The fields of the kind of comparison (type) and those of its tests (comparaisons.R: test_deux_variables).

type.description: "contingence" (two qualitative variables), "groupes" (a measurement between groups), "correlation" (two measurements) or "apparie" (a paired test).

n.description: The observations where both are known; for a paired test, the pairs.

manquantes.description: The observations left out for a missing value; for a paired test between levels, the rows of A and B without a value or a key.

tests.description: A table of the tests, as columns: test, statistique, ddl1, ddl2, p, effet and nom_effet; khi2 (V) and, when Cochran's rule fails or for a 2 × 2 table, fisher (OR for 2 × 2); welch (d) and mann_whitney (r_rb) for two groups; anova (eta2), welch_anova and kruskal (epsilon2) for more; pearson (r) and spearman (rho); t_apparie (dz) and wilcoxon (r_rb).

conseille.description: The test to read, one of tests' test.

raison.description: Why: "" (its conditions hold), "attendus" (expected counts too small for the chi-square), "normalite" (a group's or the differences' normality is doubtful, Shapiro–Wilk p < 0.05), "variances" (the variances differ, Brown–Forsythe p < 0.05), and for a paired test "nombre" (over 5,000 pairs, normality not tested), "constantes" (constant differences: no t-test) or "non_testee" (Shapiro–Wilk couldn't run).

phrase.description: The advised test's result in a sentence for a report, in the request's language; absent when erreur is given.

lignes.description: contingence: the categories of x present.

colonnes.description: contingence: the categories of y present.

effectifs.description: contingence: the counts, an array of rows.

part_attendus_faibles.description: contingence: the share of expected counts under 5.

cochran.description: contingence: whether Cochran's rule holds (no expected count under 1, at most 20 % under 5).

fisher_simule.description: contingence: whether Fisher's p was simulated (100,000 tables, beyond 2 × 2 and 200 observations).

ic_cotes.description: contingence: the 95 % interval of the odds ratio of a 2 × 2 table; null otherwise.

groupes.description: groupes: a table of the groups of 2 observations or more, as columns: groupe, n, moyenne, ecart_type, mediane, q1, q3, shapiro_p.

ecartes.description: groupes: the groups left out, with fewer than 2 observations.

variances.description: groupes: Brown and Forsythe's test of the variances, {statistique, p}.

valeurs.description: The values plotted, as columns: groupes {groupe, valeur, nom}; correlation {x, y, nom}.

difference.description: Two groups: B − A's mean difference and Welch's 95 % interval; a paired test: the mean difference B − A and its 95 % interval (null bounds for constant differences).

posthoc.description: groupes, 3 to 50 groups: the pairwise comparisons {anova: Tukey's, welch_anova: Games and Howell's, kruskal: Dunn's}, each a table: a, b, difference, bas, haut, p (Dunn's: a, b, z, p, p_ajuste by Holm).

note_comparaisons.description: Why there are no pairwise comparisons: more than 50 groups or levels, or no group holding two levels; in the request's language.

ic.description: correlation: the 95 % interval of Pearson's r.

normalite.description: correlation: Shapiro–Wilk's p of x and of y (null beyond 5,000 observations or without variation).

ordonnee.description: correlation: the intercept of the least-squares line of y on x.

ligne.description: apparie: true for two measurements paired by the observation, false for levels paired by a key.

a.description: apparie: the level A, or the first measurement's name.

b.description: apparie: the level B, or the second measurement's name.

cle.description: apparie: the key, {uid, nom, qualitative}; uid "observation" for two measurements of a row.

paires.description: apparie: the pairs, as columns: cle, a, b, difference (b − a), nom_a, nom_b (the observations' names).

sans_partenaire.description: apparie: the keys of A and of B without a partner, {a, b}.

shapiro_p.description: apparie: Shapiro–Wilk's p of the differences.

exact.description: apparie: whether Wilcoxon's p is exact (under 50 differences, none zero, no ties).

toutes.description: apparie, three levels or more: every pair of levels (or of the levels of a same group, with dans), as columns: groupe (with dans), a, b, n, difference, bas, haut, p_t, mediane, p_w, non_teste (why a pair isn't tested, "" otherwise), p_t_holm, p_w_holm.

friedman.description: apparie, three levels or more: Friedman's test of every level (one per group with dans), as columns: groupe (with dans), k, n, laissees, statistique, ddl, p, W (Kendall's), non_teste, p_holm, phrase.

sans_groupe.description: apparie with dans: the levels whose rows have no group.

dans.description: apparie with dans: the group variable, {uid, nom, qualitative}.

erreur.description: apparie, three levels or more: why the pair A–B can't be tested (fewer than three shared keys…), the table of all the pairs being given all the same; the other fields of the pair are then absent.

erreurs.message: Choose two different variables
erreurs.quand: x and y are the same.

erreurs.message: Each variable needs at least two categories in these observations
erreurs.quand: Two qualitative variables, one of which has a single category where both are known.

erreurs.message: At least two groups of two observations or more are needed
erreurs.quand: A measurement between groups, with fewer than two groups of two observations.

erreurs.message: At least three observations with both variables known are needed
erreurs.quand: Two measurements known together on fewer than three observations.

erreurs.message: A paired test compares a measurement between two levels of a qualitative variable, or two measurements of the same observation
erreurs.quand: appariement with two qualitative variables.

erreurs.message: Two measurements are paired by the observation: the same row holds both values
erreurs.quand: Two measurements, and appariement isn't "observation".

erreurs.message: At least three pairs are needed: only <n> observation(s) have both values
erreurs.quand: Two measurements paired by the observation, known together on fewer than three rows.

erreurs.message: A measurement and groups are paired by a third variable (the year, for two sectors)
erreurs.quand: appariement is "observation" for a measurement and a qualitative variable.

erreurs.message: The pairing key must be a third variable
erreurs.quand: appariement is x or y.

erreurs.message: The group of the pairs must be a fourth variable
erreurs.quand: dans is x, y or appariement.

erreurs.message: Pairs are grouped by a qualitative variable or an ID
erreurs.quand: dans is a quantitative variable.

erreurs.message: Two different levels are needed to compare
erreurs.quand: niveaux doesn't name two different levels present.

erreurs.message: At least three pairs are needed: <A> and <B> share only <n> value(s) of <key>
erreurs.quand: The levels A and B share fewer than three keys, and there is no table of all the pairs (two levels, or more than 50); when there is one, this comes back in erreur.

erreurs.message: <level> has rows for several values of <group> (<values>): a level must belong to a single group
erreurs.quand: With dans, a level's rows are in several groups.

erreurs.message: <A> and <B> have the same value in every pair: nothing to compare
erreurs.quand: Every difference of the pairs is zero.

test_deux_variables.effet_detail: A paired test between the levels of a variable that has three levels or more keeps the table of all its pairs in the session (20 tables at most, by project, data revision and language), so that choosing other levels A and B doesn't compute it again; nothing else changes.

niveaux.but: Gives the levels that the observations have of a qualitative variable or an identifier, in the order of the tests, which a paired test offers for A and B.

niveaux.description: The levels with at least one observation (always an array): a variable's categories in their order, an identifier's values in the order of numbers when they are numbers, else of text.

erreurs.message: This variable is not qualitative
erreurs.quand: variable is a quantitative variable.

baci.but: Gives the series of the gaps between the impact and the control units' means over time and, with an event, tests the gaps after it against those before (before–after control–impact, BACI).

y.description: The response: a quantitative variable's number.

temps.description: The time: a variable's number or "id:k" (not "id:1"), made of numbers (the year) or of dates, read as decimal years.

unite.description: The unit (the sector): a qualitative variable's number or "id:k" (not "id:1").

impact.description: The impact units: levels of unite.

temoins.description: The control units: other levels of unite.

evenement.description: The first time counted after: a number for a time made of numbers; a number (its 1 January) or a date for a time made of dates. Without it, the series of the gaps only.

fin.description: With evenement: the last time of the after period, included (later times stay out of the test): a number, or a date for a time made of dates.

test.description: The test of the gaps after against those before.

resultat.description: comparaisons.R: baci; the fields from periodes on come only with evenement.

dates.description: Whether the time is made of dates: times are then decimal years.

impact.description: The impact units, without repeats (a single string for one unit).

temoins.description: The control units, without repeats (a single string for one unit).

serie.description: A table, as columns, of the times where the impact and the controls both have values: temps, impact and temoins (the means of their rows), n_impact, n_temoins, ecart (impact − temoins) and, with evenement, periode ("avant", "apres", or "hors" after fin).

seuls.description: The times where only the impact, or only the controls, have values: {impact, temoins}.

manquantes.description: The rows of impact or control units without a value or a time.

repetees.description: A table of the units that have several rows at a time, as columns: unite, temps (at how many times); null when none has.

periodes.description: A table of the periods avant and apres, as columns: periode, n, debut, fin, moyenne, ecart_type, mediane, shapiro_p (of their gaps).

tests.description: A table of the three tests, as columns: test (welch, student, mann_whitney), statistique, ddl1, ddl2, p, effet, nom_effet (d, d, r_rb), bas, haut (the 95 % interval of the change).

difference.description: The mean gap after minus before, and its 95 % interval (Student's for student, else Welch's).

evenement.description: The event, as a number (a decimal year for dates).

fin.description: The end of the after period, or null.

hors.description: The times after fin, left out of the test.

temps_unites.description: The smallest number of times of an impact or control unit, up to fin (with three or more, the view's mixed model takes CAR1 by default).

repetees_modele.description: repetees among the rows the mixed model would take (up to fin): CAR1 needs one time per unit.

phrase.description: The chosen test's result in a sentence for a report, in the request's language.

modeles.description: The BACI mixed models of the same settings (with or without CAR1) fitted in the session (baci_modele), oldest first, each {id, nom, car1, estimation, erreur_type, ddl, t, p, bas, haut, phrase}: the period × impact coefficient, the BACI effect (always an array).

erreurs.message: The response, the time and the unit must be three different variables
erreurs.quand: Two of y, temps and unite are the same.

erreurs.message: The response must be a quantitative variable
erreurs.quand: y is qualitative, or an identifier.

erreurs.message: The unit must be a qualitative variable or an ID
erreurs.quand: unite is quantitative.

erreurs.message: Choose at least one impact unit and one control unit
erreurs.quand: impact or temoins is empty.

erreurs.message: <unit> has no level <levels>
erreurs.quand: impact or temoins names a level the unit doesn't have.

erreurs.message: A unit can't be both impact and control: <units>
erreurs.quand: A level is in both impact and temoins.

erreurs.message: No value of <time> where both the impact and the controls have a value of <y>
erreurs.quand: The impact and the controls never have values at the same time.

erreurs.message: The event time must be a number or a date
erreurs.quand: evenement is neither.

erreurs.message: The end of the after period must be a number or a date
erreurs.quand: fin is neither.

erreurs.message: The time (<time>) is made of numbers: enter the event as a number (2008), not a date
erreurs.quand: A date as evenement for a time made of numbers (likewise for fin: enter the end as a number (2012), not a date).

erreurs.message: The time (<time>) is made of dates: enter the end as a date (31/12/2012); a year alone would be its 1 January
erreurs.quand: A number as fin for a time made of dates.

erreurs.message: The end of the after period (<end>) comes before the event (<event>)
erreurs.quand: fin < evenement.

erreurs.message: At least two values of <time> are needed in each period, before and after <event>: there are <n> before and <n> after
erreurs.quand: A period has fewer than two times with a gap.

erreurs.message: The gap is the same at every time: nothing to compare
erreurs.quand: Every gap of the two periods is equal.

series.but: Gives a variable's values over time in long format, by line and panel, with each panel's mean at each time and, with tendances, each line's trend test.

temps.description: The time: a variable's number or "id:k" (not "id:1"), made of numbers (the year) or of dates, read as decimal years.

lignes.description: What makes the lines (the sector): a qualitative variable's number or "id:k" (not "id:1"); absent or "": one line.

panneaux.description: What makes the panels (the site), likewise; absent or "": one panel.

tendances.description: true for each line's trend: the Mann–Kendall test and Sen's slope, or the seasonal Kendall test with saisons.

correction.description: With tendances: the correction of the p-values over the lines tested; another value comes back as tendances_erreur.

autocorrelation.description: With tendances: Hamed and Rao's (1998) correction of the Mann–Kendall test for autocorrelation (not with saisons).

saisons.description: With tendances only: the seasonal Kendall test, the season of each point being "mois" (the month of a time made of dates), a qualitative variable's number or "id:k" (not "id:1"); absent or "": none.

resultat.description: series.R: series_variable, and tendances_series with tendances.

dates.description: Whether the time is made of dates: the times are then decimal years (2019.37), which the interface shows as dates.

lignes.description: What makes the lines, {uid, nom}; null for one line.

panneaux.description: What makes the panels, {uid, nom}; null for one panel.

points.description: A table, as columns, of the observations whose time and value are known (and their line and panel), sorted by panel, line and time: temps, valeur, ligne, panneau (null without lines or panels), uid, nom, and saison with saisons.

niveaux_lignes.description: The lines' levels, in their order (always an array, empty for one line).

niveaux_panneaux.description: The panels' levels, in their order (always an array).

moyennes.description: A table, as columns, of the mean of each panel's lines at each time: panneau, temps, valeur, n.

sans_temps_valeur.description: The observations left out for a missing time or value.

sans_groupe.description: Those left out for a missing line or panel.

doubles.description: The times that come twice in a line (not a series: finer lines needed): {n}, and with n > 0 the first one's ligne, panneau and temps.

saisons.description: With tendances and saisons: what makes the seasons, {uid, nom} (uid "mois" for the months).

sans_saison.description: With tendances and saisons: the points without a season, left out of the test.

tendances.description: With tendances: a table, as columns, one row per line of each panel: panneau, ligne, n, debut, fin, test (mann_kendall, hamed_rao or saisonnier), pente (Sen's, per unit of time, per year for dates), bas and haut (its 95 % interval), tau, S, var_S, p, n_n_etoile (Hamed and Rao's n/n*), saisons and medianes (the seasonal test's), non_teste (why a line isn't tested, "" otherwise: fewer than 4 times…), p_ajuste; an empty object when no point is left.

tendances_erreur.description: With tendances: why the trends' options were refused, the series coming without trends (a status 200): Unknown correction: <correction>; Seasons by month of the year need a time made of dates; Seasons are made by a qualitative variable or an ID; The seasonal test takes the seasons as independent: Hamed and Rao's correction for autocorrelation doesn't apply to it; or a seasons variable not found.

rarefaction.but: Gives the rarefaction of each observation's species counts, the species accumulation over the observations and the richness estimators, overall or by group.

especes.description: The species: the numbers of two quantitative variables or more, counts of individuals (one row per observation).

groupe.description: A qualitative variable's number or "id:k" (not "id:1"): an accumulation curve and estimators per group.

taille.description: The common size the richness is rarefied to, rounded; the smallest total of an observation by default (also for a value under 1).

pas.description: The step of the rarefaction curves; by default the largest total over 100, rounded up (about 100 points a curve).

resultat.description: rarefaction.R: rarefaction_projet, as vegan's rarefy, rarecurve, specaccum (exact), estimateR and specpool compute them.

n.description: The observations kept: every count known (and the group, with groupe).

entiers.description: Whether the counts are whole numbers (to 1e-8): the rarefaction, Chao1 and ACE need them (null in the tables, and courbes null, otherwise).

taille.description: The common size of the rarefaction.

taille_min.description: The smallest total of an observation with individuals (the default size).

manquantes.description: The observations left out for a missing count.

sans_groupe.description: Those left out for a missing group.

vides.description: The observations without any individual: no rarefaction, but they count in the accumulation.

petites.description: The observations whose total is under taille: no rarefied richness.

groupe.description: What makes the groups, {uid, nom}; null without groupe.

niveaux.description: The groups (always an array, empty without groupe).

observations.description: A table, as columns, one row per observation kept: uid, nom, groupe, N (individuals), S (species), Sm and se (the richness rarefied to taille and its standard deviation), chao1, se_chao1, ace, se_ace (Chao1 corrected for bias, ACE).

courbes.description: The rarefaction curves of the observations with individuals, a table as columns: uid, taille (1, 1 + pas… and their total), S, se, and _row (row names jsonlite writes, without meaning); null without whole counts.

accumulation.description: The exact species accumulation over 1 to n observations (per group), a table as columns: groupe, sites, richesse, et (its standard deviation).

estimateurs.description: The estimators of the richness from the presences, a table as columns, one row per group (one row without groupe): groupe, n, S, chao, se_chao, jack1, se_jack1, jack2, boot, se_boot.

carte.but: Gives each observation's coordinates and their WGS 84 longitude and latitude, for the map (Plots › Map).

projet.description: The project's id; its coordinates must be set.

uid.description: The observations' numbers, all of them in the data's order.

nom.description: Their names.

x.description: Their x in the project's system (null where missing).

lon.description: Their WGS 84 longitude; null for plane coordinates ("plan") and missing values.

systeme.description: {code: the EPSG code or "plan"; nom: its name, in the request's language for "plan"; type: lonlat, lcc, tm, laea, merc or plan}.

autocorrelation_spatiale.but: Measures the spatial autocorrelation of a variable or of a regression's residuals with Moran's I, its correlogram and the semivariogram (Plots › Spatial autocorrelation).

modele.description: A fitted model's id: its residuals, or with variable that variable on the model's observations; its project is the one used.

projet.description: Without modele, the project's id (its coordinates must be set).

variable.description: The number of a quantitative variable; without it, the regression's residuals (modele needed).

valeurs.standardises: Those of the model's views: standardized, deviance residuals for mgcv, normalized with CAR1.
valeurs.quantiles: The randomized quantile residuals of a count, presence-absence, positive or proportion model.

voisinage.description: The spatial weights (spatial.R: poids_spatiaux), {methode: voisins (the k nearest neighbours, made mutual; the default), bande (1 up to portee, by default the smallest distance that gives each observation a neighbour) or inverse (1/d, up to portee when given); k: 4 by default, kept between 1 and n − 1; portee: in metres; standardiser: false keeps the weights as they are, otherwise each row sums to 1}.

permutations.description: The permutations of Moran's test, from a fixed seed (kept within 0 to 9999; 0: none).

classes.description: The correlogram's distance classes, of equal width up to half the largest distance (kept within 2 to 30).

par_lieu.description: Replace the values of the observations at the same place by their mean, one per place; otherwise their zero distances make them nearest neighbours.

resultat.description: Distances are in metres: along great circles for longitudes and latitudes, straight for plane coordinates.

nom.description: The variable's name, or residuals or quantile residuals, in the request's language.

n.description: The values tested (the places, with par_lieu).

observations.description: The observations with coordinates and a value.

laissees.description: Those left out, without coordinates or a value.

uid.description: The observations tested (with par_lieu, the first of each place).

valeurs.description: Their values (with par_lieu, each place's mean).

nulles.description: The pairs of observations at a zero distance.

lieux.description: With par_lieu, the number of observations at each place; null otherwise.

voisinage.description: The weights used: {methode, k (null but for voisins), portee (the distance used; null for voisins, and for inverse without one), standardiser, voisins: the mean number of neighbours, sans_voisin: the observations without one}.

moran.description: Moran's I under randomization, as spdep::moran.test: {I, esperance, variance, z, p (one-sided, for a positive autocorrelation), n, S0}, with permutations {permutations, p_permutations, as spdep::moran.mc}; for the residuals of a linear model without random effects, modele, the test that accounts for its fit, as spdep::lm.morantest {I, esperance, variance, z, p, n, rang}.

correlogramme.description: A table (columns): classe, de, a (its bounds), distance (the mean of its pairs), paires, I, esperance, z, p (two-sided) and p_holm (corrected over the classes); null values for a class without pairs.

variogramme.description: The empirical semivariogram, as gstat::variogram (15 classes up to a third of the points' bounding diagonal), a table (columns): classe, de, a, paires, distance, gamma; only the classes with pairs.

distance_max.description: The largest distance between two observations tested.

systeme.description: The coordinates' system: an EPSG code or "plan".

chemin.description: The file to write, its extension its format; without it, a file named after the project in a new folder of the engine's temporary folder.

journal.description: The entries the code added: the command, then its outputs, warnings, error and plots (always an array). An error stops the code there and is an entry, not an error of the request.

modifies.description: The ids of the projects the code replaced (P1 <- …), whose summaries the interface asks again (always an array).

completer.but: Gives the names that can complete the word before the cursor in the R console, without evaluating anything.

curseur.description: The cursor's place: the number of characters of texte before it; the end of texte by default.

modele.description: The model shown, bound to m as console binds it (an unknown id is ignored).

projet.description: The project shown, bound to p (an unknown id is ignored).

debut.description: The number of characters before the word completed: where the candidate replaces it.

candidats.description: The names that start with it, 300 at most (always an array): after x$ or x[[", the object's elements; in a call's brackets, its arguments ("name = ") first; else the console's objects, the engine's and R's functions.
